  • design.md

    Does: Commits the project to its load-bearing technical bets, several of them corrected in place and in the first person as the author learned. The bets: browser-grammar parsing with every recovery fatal, JSON Schema authored as the source of truth with typify-generated types as a convenience only, a formatter that never rewraps prose, visualization source as visible content rendered into a sibling, and committed vendored assets verified by a Nix lockfile check. It also orders the work so the two riskiest bets and the closed vocabulary are tested before anything hardens around them. The in-place corrections: 'from the schema alone' was too strong, a schema version buys identifiability rather than cheap migration, and the specs no longer claim diff minimality.

  • evidence/diff-locality.md

    Does: Measures six content edits by changed diff bytes against minimal edit bytes. For example, one 7-byte edit costs 225 bytes on a one-line paragraph and 85 when broken per sentence, with the same one-line count either way. It concludes that diff locality is owned by the author's line breaks, that position within a line does not matter (225 vs 227, so nothing is rewrapped), and that the only carry-forward is unenforced guidance: break prose at sentence boundaries. It is the number behind deterministic-formatting's 'Formatting introduces no diff churn' disclaimer, the design's 'The formatter never rewraps text', and task 5.8.

    disposition: carried

2026-08-13-content-address-runtime-assets

Records version 0.1.0. This change replaced the project's one-copy-per-document asset layout with a content-addressed store, `assets/sha256-<16 hex>/<filename>`. Documents now reference the exact bytes they were authored against, and asset topology became something the project checks: each reference is resolved per document, and duplication is checked across the whole project by a new `self-assets` step in `scripts/check`. It was needed because an archived document had shipped a stylesheet copy that was stale from the day it was written: its skip link did nothing. Two accepted document-template scenarios, 'Shared assets' and 'Runtime version is recorded', could not both hold under the old mutable `assets/vendor/` layout, and no check noticed. The evidence shows the build doing slightly less than the specs promise. The original defect's shape, a reference naming no hash, still passes validation and is caught only by `format --check`.

Collapsed specification. Two groups, one per capability, and document-template first. It defines what a stored asset and a reference are, and says initialization must write them. document-validation's three requirements enforce those definitions. Inside document-validation, keep the source order (reference rule, duplication rule, check-suite wiring), because the third requirement names the first two. Neither group has a Purpose to introduce it, so each gets only a heading naming its capability.

Purpose statements. Neither delta carries a `## Purpose`. There is no non-requirement content to account for.

Change subject. Yes. Read alone, the two deltas show a modified runtime requirement, a modified init requirement, and three new validation rules. Nothing in them says that the project moved from per-document `assets/vendor/<file>` copies to a store at `assets/sha256-<16 hex>/<filename>`, rewrote existing references, re-rendered the archived deterministic-formatting.html so its skip link works, and deleted the duplicated trees. The statement would say: each runtime asset is now stored once under an address derived from its bytes and referenced by that address, so 'Shared assets' and 'Runtime version is recorded' both hold; asset references are resolved per document and duplication is checked per project by the check suite. Its sources are proposal 'What Changes' and group-8-verification.md sections 8.2 and 8.5.

Built differs from stated. (1) References naming no hash. Scenario 'An asset reference identifies its bytes' and the first validation requirement assume every reference names a hash. As built, an unaddressed reference such as `assets/htmlspec.css` resolves to `NotAddressed` and no `asset/*` rule fires (`an_unaddressed_reference_is_not_this_rules_business`, group-3-decision.md). `format --check` rejects it as non-canonical instead (group-8-verification.md section 8.4). The original defect's shape passes `htmlspec validate` and fails the suite only through the formatter. (2) Scope. The scenario 'Document validated with no store present' uses 'a conformance fixture whose references are symbolic' as its example. As built, the store is the nearest ancestor holding `assets/` (`store_for`, group-3-decision.md). Fixtures validated from inside the repository are therefore in scope, and pass only because their references are unaddressed. Only the conformance harness supplies no store. (3) Duplication. The delta says 'Validation SHALL reject a project'. As built, a separate command, `htmlspec assets`, evaluates it, with rule `asset/duplicate`, wired into `scripts/check` as `self-assets`. `htmlspec validate` accepts a document in a duplicated project (group-8-verification.md section 8.4). (4) Formatter. Tasks 5.1–5.4 built fill-only-absent reference rewriting pinned by a fixture, and no requirement in either delta states it. (5) This one comes from the code at commit 86c33f4, not from the tasks or evidence: `Store::resolve` matches on the 16-hex prefix of the stored bytes' digest and reads only the reference's last two path components ('however deep the document sits'). A reference at the wrong relative depth, which would not render offline, still resolves. The delta says only 'resolve to stored bytes', so this is a detail the delta leaves open rather than a direct contradiction.

Evidence and verification units. Verification is recorded and could be cited, not manufactured. group-8-verification.md gives commands and exit codes that map onto specific scenarios: 'Reference to bytes the project does not store' (asset/unresolved, exit 1); 'Stored bytes do not match the name' plus the distinguishability statement (asset/mismatch, with unresolved firing zero times); 'Duplicate copies of one library' (asset/duplicate, exit 1); 'Per-document validation is not sufficient' (assets exit 1, validate exit 0); 'Shared assets' and 'One store serving many documents' (`htmlspec assets .`, each of 8 once); and the check-suite requirement (7 steps, `self-assets` red then green). group-3-decision.md names the tests pinning 'Mismatch cannot be downgraded' and 'Document validated with no store present', but records their existence and a passing suite, not a per-test result. No recorded result exists for 'Upgrading a library', 'Two documents needing different bytes of one file', 'A document cannot exempt itself', or the init scenarios: tasks 3.6, 4.4 and 6.x say tests or fixtures were added, and nothing records their output. Section 8.3 (the skip-link check) verifies the proposal's defect fix, which corresponds to no requirement in these deltas. The coordinator decides whether to create evidence or verification units. This reader only reports that real records exist for the scenarios listed.

Decided. Convention 8 (The hand-converted documents cross as they are today): deterministic-formatting.html crosses with its current bytes into evidence/documents/, outside promotion's checks, so its two missing stylesheets hold nothing back. Confirmed at 139b206: both directories are still absent from assets/. The 9c3a3c7 deletion is history and is not repaired. The reader asked: Another slice's central decision needs a fact from this one. The file this change re-rendered, `openspec/changes/archive/2026-08-10-html-spec/documents/deterministic-formatting.html` (tasks 7.1–7.3, group-8-verification.md section 8.3), references `../../../../../assets/sha256-3e4014c3004abea5/htmlspec.css` and `.../sha256-da53340d33da116e/htmlspec-print.css`. Neither directory exists in `assets/` today. `git log --diff-filter=D` shows commit 9c3a3c7 (Separate a change into four artifact kinds) deleted them. That runs against this change's decision 'Never collect unreferenced assets' and its delta's 'Replacing a library SHALL add a location and leave existing locations intact'. The skip-link fix this change verified no longer renders from the repository. This slice decides nothing about that file.

They could be rewritten to their `htmlspec/` destinations or kept as historical text. The contract is silent.

2026-08-14-separate-artifact-kinds

Records version 0.1.0. This change recovered OpenSpec's separation of a change into stages. The port had flattened it into one optional-everything document shape carrying a required `status` field that no rule read. It replaced `status` with a required, undefaulted, closed `kind` (proposal, design, tasks, specification). It enforced exactly three kind rules: two errors, plus one advisory `review/*` warning that `--strict` cannot promote. Proposal and design were left unconstrained and pinned by positive fixtures, and archival became an agent-written specification that the program only validates. Its evidence measures the migration of 69 documents and five mutation runs. Its `documents/` directory holds the project's first change authored in its own format (task 10.5), which found the cost of the four-document model: the task-to-requirement reference could no longer be checked by a tool.

Collapsed specification. Suggested (the arrangement is the agent's): one group per capability in the proposal's order, the new capability first (artifact-kinds, 8), then document-template (1), document-validation (4) and toolchain-packaging (2). Introduce each group with its proposal.md Capabilities sentence, cited as the source. Grouping by capability keeps each requirement next to the accepted specification it merges into on sync. That matters because the delta states four obligations twice, in different capabilities, and each restatement goes to a different accepted spec. Cross-link the pairs rather than merging them: completeness ('A tasks document carries the workable items' / 'A tasks document must carry at least one task'); placement ('A specification states the settled contract as built' / 'A specification must not carry task units'); contract rules (the last paragraph of 'A proposal argues value and the tool does not shape it' / 'The contract rules apply to every kind'); archival ('Archival produces the specification and then updates the accepted contract' / 'Archival produces the specification and updates the accepted contract').

Purpose statements. None of the four deltas has a ## Purpose. The closest thing is proposal.md's '## Capabilities' section, which gives the author's own sentence for each: artifact-kinds (new) 'Defines the four artifact kinds…'; document-template (modified) 'Replaces the per-document lifecycle status with a declared artifact kind…'; document-validation (modified) 'Adds the placement error…, the completeness error…, and the advisory warning…'; toolchain-packaging (modified) '`init` accepts a kind and can create a complete change directory. Archival gains an agent-driven operation…'. The accepted artifact-kinds Purpose closely paraphrases the proposal's artifact-kinds line.

Change subject. Yes. Each delta states only its own capability's changes, and none says what the change did as a whole. The collapsed specification needs a sentence saying so, for example: it replaced the per-document `status` with a required, undefaulted, closed `kind`; enforced exactly three kind rules, two errors and one advisory review warning; left proposal and design unconstrained; made a change a directory of kinded documents; and made archival an agent-produced specification gated by validation. All of this is sourced from proposal.md's 'Why' and 'What Changes'.

Built differs from stated. Three places. (1) document-template's scenario 'A document declaring a lifecycle status → validation reports it': I found no implementation. Nothing in crates/, conformance/ or fixtures/ reads `htmlspec-status`, projection.md §9 projects only version and kind, and no task adds the report. This is by search, not by running (see that entity's open question). (2) artifact-kinds' 'A specification states the settled contract as built' says a specification 'SHALL carry requirement, scenario, evidence, and verification units', but what was built enforces only the three rules, so a specification missing those units is valid. (3) Some built facts appear in no delta, though none contradicts one: init defaults to `proposal` (documents/tasks.html); init ships four templates, one per kind (documents/design.html, measured-claims.md §1); the rule identifiers are kind/task-in-specification, kind/no-tasks and review/unverified-requirement (measured-claims.md §2, and still present in crates/htmlspec-validate/src/rules/kinds.rs and review.rs); the archival check reads only the specification file (measured-claims.md §6); and a seventh fixture covers a document declaring no kind (measured-claims.md §1).

Evidence and verification units. Unlike many changes, this one's evidence does record verification that can be cited per requirement. mutation-testing.txt names the tests that failed when each rule was broken, and measured-claims.md §3–§6 records runs. Records exist for: 'A specification must not carry task units' (mutation 1; §6 archival stop); 'A tasks document must carry at least one task' (mutation 2); 'A specification requirement without verification is reported as incomplete' (mutations 3–4; §5); 'A proposal argues value and the tool does not shape it' (§4); 'A document declares its identity and provenance', missing-kind scenario only (mutation 5, the_schema_enumerates_exactly_the_four_artifact_kinds); both archival requirements (§6's nine archive.rs tests, the_archive_operation_ships_no_requirement_extractor); and 'A single command exposes validate, format, and init' (every_kind_init_can_produce_validates_immediately, init_change_creates_a_valid_change_directory). I found no run record for 'Every synthesis and every contract update is agent-driven' (the partial-merge scenarios), 'A design reasons in whatever form the reasoning takes' (a positive fixture exists per task 7.5, but no evidence records a run), 'Intended content is guidance…', 'The contract rules apply to every kind', or the lifecycle-status scenario. Whether verification units should cite these evidence records, or be omitted as having no delta counterpart, is for the coordinator. If they are omitted, review/unverified-requirement will warn on each of the 15 migrated requirements. The warnings never gate.

Decided. Decision 2 (Scenario identifiers that collide): both 'A tasks document carrying other units' scenarios derive from requirement heading plus scenario heading, recorded as scenario: notes. No suffixing is used. The reader asked: Scenario identifier collision. 'A tasks document carrying other units' is the heading of a scenario in both the artifact-kinds delta (under 'A tasks document carries the workable items') and the document-validation delta (under 'A tasks document must carry at least one task'). The WHEN clauses are identical; the THEN reasons differ slightly. Collapsed into one specification.html, identifiers derived from these headings would collide, and document-schema's 'Every semantic unit has a stable unique identifier' makes duplicate identifiers invalid. The migrate skill's derivation rules speak about requirement headings; I found nothing that decides how two scenarios with one heading get distinct identifiers.

2026-08-17-project-bootstrap-cli

Records version 0.1.0. This change made the project, not the document, the subject of htmlspec's first command. Before it, `htmlspec init` demanded a path, gave every change its own 6 MB runtime store, and `htmlspec assets` could not see the duplicate stores it had just made. After it, `init` sets up `htmlspec/` with one asset store, installs agent instructions for five tools, and writes `spec.nix`. Document and change creation moved to `new`. Archival refuses unless the declared version has advanced. An ascending asset reference with no store above it is reported, and a cancelled prompt exits with a fourth exit code. Two things were not built as the deltas state them: the `spec.nix` pin (written as `null`, read by a subset parser rather than by Nix) and the version gate (as archived, it read versions from directory names that nothing wrote).

Collapsed specification. One group per capability, project-bootstrap first because it is the change's subject, then toolchain-packaging, then document-validation. Within project-bootstrap, keep the delta's own order, which already runs from what a project is, through declaration and gate and resolution, to installation, selection, re-run, and exit. Two obligations are stated from both sides across capabilities, and a short note in each group should say so: cancellation ('A declined or interrupted operation is distinguishable from a failure' in project-bootstrap, and 'Exit codes distinguish outcomes' in toolchain-packaging), and JSON suppressing prompts (the 'Structured output requested' scenario in project-bootstrap, and 'Output is available in human and machine forms' in toolchain-packaging). Fourteen requirements in all: 10 added, 3 modified in toolchain-packaging (one of them also renamed), and 1 modified in document-validation. None removed.

Purpose statements. None of the three deltas carries a ## Purpose. project-bootstrap is a new capability and its delta opens directly with ## ADDED Requirements. The accepted spec then received the OpenSpec placeholder 'TBD - created by archiving change project-bootstrap-cli. Update Purpose after archive.' toolchain-packaging and document-validation are modified capabilities whose Purpose lives only in the accepted spec. The only authored statement of what project-bootstrap is for is the proposal's 'New Capabilities' bullet ('Defines what an htmlspec project is — a declared root, one asset store, and a directory shape — how commands find it from a subdirectory, and the bootstrap operation that establishes it...').

Change subject. Yes. No delta says what the change did as a whole. The only trace is the RENAMED paragraph's 'init used to create one document, and its subject is now the project'. A reader of the specification alone could not tell that `init` was repurposed, that `new` took over document creation, or that the store moved from per-change to per-project. A statement along these lines is needed: 'This change made the project, rather than the document, the subject of htmlspec's first command. `init` establishes a project with one asset store, installs agent instructions, and writes a declaration whose version archival requires to advance. `new` creates documents and changes. An ascending asset reference with no store above it is now reported.'

Built differs from stated. Two places. (1) project-bootstrap, 'A project declares its name, version, and expected toolchain': the delta says the declaration is in the build's language 'so that the pinned program reference is a build input rather than a value a bespoke parser must interpret', and its scenario 'The pinned program is a build input' says it 'resolves as a build input, with no separate parser'. As built, `init` writes `htmlspec = null;` and no command reads the pin (evidence/testing-state-2026-08-17.md §6 item 4). The reader is a hand-written strict-subset parser, not Nix evaluation, because shelling out to Nix would break the standalone-artifact requirement (evidence/first-run.md 'The packaged artifact'; module doc of crates/htmlspec-cli/src/declaration.rs). The accepted spec still carries the delta's wording unchanged. (2) project-bootstrap, 'Archival requires the project version to advance': as archived, the gate read the last archived version from the archive directory's name (task 9.1's choice; `archived_version` in commands.rs at 77054b9). Nothing wrote versioned names, and this change's own directory has none, so the gate always compared against 0.0.0. It refused only an unmoved 0.0.0 and never a later unadvanced version, until 2026-08-30-finish-the-archival switched to VERSION files. This comes from the code history and a later change's code comment, not from this change's evidence, which tested the gate only against a fresh project. The coordinator should decide whether 'records what was built' reaches this. The init→new spelling (`new document <kind> <path>` as built against `new <kind> <path>` in the proposal and tasks) does not conflict with any delta, which states creation abstractly.

Evidence and verification units. Verification records exist and could be cited, in evidence files, not in any delta. evidence/testing-state-2026-08-17.md §2 names six integration tests, one per refusal path of 'Archival requires the project version to advance' (crates/htmlspec-cli/tests/archive.rs:379-474). evidence/first-run.md names init_does_not_block_when_no_terminal_is_attached (the 'No terminal available' scenario) and records exit 3 for cancellation. evidence/asset-footprint.md names the_asset_check_reports_duplication_between_two_stores (the 'Checking a project's assets' scenario). Tasks 14.3-14.5 record that scripts/check-prompt drives the real prompt, covers exit 3, and was confirmed to fail with either guard removed, but only as task text, not as a measured record. Evidence units have direct sources: the six evidence files. Whether verification units derived from these records count as 'derived from a record' or as manufactured is the coordinator's call under project-migration's 'A unit kind the source format has none of'. None exists in the deltas themselves.

Rename. A single command exposes validate, format, and init → A single command exposes validate, format, bootstrap, and create. Author's reason: The requirement's subject changed rather than its topic. `init` used to create one document, and its subject is now the project, so a requirement naming `init` alongside `validate` and `format` no longer describes the command surface. The rename is stated rather than implied, because a MODIFIED block cannot find a header that moved.

Mapped. project-migration's "A source change's own configuration is surveyed, and its predecessor becomes its declaration": the survey reports configuration null for this change, so it has no file, which is a different fact from a file that names no predecessor, and the migrated change has no FOLLOWS. The directory holds no runbooks.json and no documents/ (confirmed by listing). The reader asked: This slice has no `.openspec.yaml`, no `runbooks.json`, and no `documents/*.html`. Nothing needs a central decision for those.

Mapped. project-migration's "A source task is carried in the state its record supports": task 8.2 is done, its words as written, with a deviation paragraph saying the declaration is read by a strict-subset parser rather than evaluated through Nix, because the standalone artifact may not need Nix at runtime, and linking evidence/first-run.md ('The packaged artifact'), a record the change carries. The destination now expresses this, so it is not recorded as open. The reader asked: Task 8.2 ([x], but not built as written) is a task-state distinction that the destination's done/dropped vocabulary cannot express. Record it as open, per 'A source distinction the destination cannot express is recorded as open, not mapped to the nearest state'.

Mapped. project-migration's "A source task is carried in the state its record supports": the deviation crosses as task 8.2's deviation paragraph, linking evidence/first-run.md. The design is preserved as written and gains nothing (convention 2). The reader asked: evidence/first-run.md points at a design deviation that the archived design does not contain. Whether the migrated design may gain it is undecided, and no requirement settles it. The default under 'Name the requirement, or name the silence' is to preserve the design as it was.

Mapped. project-migration's "Migrated archives carry their versions where the archival gate reads them" (scenario "Several source changes sharing one version"): VERSION 0.1.0 crosses unchanged onto each of the seven changes that share it, and CHANGELOG.md's '0.1.0 — the first release' entry, which names all seven and calls itself a reconstruction, is still in the repository at 139b206 and stays where it is, per the plan's release-record rule. The retroactive origin (41310f8) is what that entry already says. The reader asked: The VERSION file was written retroactively (2026-08-21, commit 41310f8). At archival, the change's own gate put versions in directory names. Carrying the VERSION file is correct under 'Migrated archives carry their versions where the archival gate reads them'. The plan should say that the recorded value is a reconstruction, and carry the CHANGELOG 0.1.0 entry with it.

Mapped. project-migration's "A source rename is carried as the heading the requirement replaced", with project-migration's "Identifiers are derived once and every reference resolves through that derivation": this change's requirement carries the TO heading with a renamed-from paragraph stating 'A single command exposes validate, format, and init', and resolves to req-a-single-command-exposes-validate-format-and-init, as do 2026-08-10-html-spec, 2026-08-14-separate-artifact-kinds, 2026-08-30-finish-the-archival, every later change that restates the requirement without renaming it, and the accepted toolchain-packaging; the plan's Identifiers rule records this one chain. The reader asked: The rename chain (A in 2026-08-10, B here, C in 2026-08-30) must resolve to one identifier, req-a-single-command-exposes-validate-format-and-init, in every document of every change in the chain. No derivation collision exists inside this change's collapsed specification: its fourteen headings are distinct.

Decided. Decision 3 (project-bootstrap's purpose): the placeholder is replaced by a summary written from the specification's own requirements, marked in the document as text the source did not contain. The reader asked: The project-bootstrap capability has no authored Purpose anywhere except the proposal's capability bullet. The accepted spec's Purpose is a placeholder. The migration has no rule for whether a placeholder Purpose is converted as is, flagged, or replaced from the proposal.

    Does: Turns the proposal into thirteen decisions, organized around a parse-at-the-boundary `ProjectRoot` type and a pure `bootstrap(&ProjectRoot, &Selection)` with the `inquire` prompt isolated above it. Each decision names what it rejected and why, often against OpenSpec 1.7.0's own code. It also records two self-corrections: the deferred `spec.nix` is reinstated because the version gate gives it a consumer, and a difference test becomes an ordering because a difference test accepts a downgrade.

    disposition: converted

    Format: Section 'Context', the four binding constraints: a short list. Keep it.

    Format: Section 'Goals / Non-Goals': two plain lists. Keep them.

    Format: Section 'Decisions': thirteen `###` decisions, each with a chosen option, its rationale, and often explicit 'Rejected:' alternatives. These fit decision units with status accepted, with the rejected options kept in the rationale. This is the design kind's optional capacity (artifact-kinds 'A design reasons in whatever form the reasoning takes'). The prose between them carries the argument and must stay continuous.

    Format: Decision 'Interaction is a decision, then a prompt that produces one': the layering is an ASCII-art diagram in a code block (lines 55-61), drawn that way because Markdown had nothing better. Make it a Mermaid flowchart: resolve_from_flags(&Args) and prompt(&mut dyn Interaction) [inquire lives here] each produce Selection, which feeds bootstrap(&ProjectRoot, &Selection) -> Outcome [no terminal].

    Format: Decision 'Deciding whether to prompt at all': the text says 'Three conditions, all required', then adds `--json` as a fourth in a later paragraph. Task 7.3 lists all four. Make it a four-row table (Condition / Absent means / Why), so the fourth condition sits with the other three instead of three paragraphs later.

    Format: Decision 'The tool table is data, and its shape is a sum type': the Rust block is code. Keep it verbatim. The five-entry line ('Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, AGENTS.md') should stay a sentence. A tool/directory/delivery table would need delivery values this design never states for each tool, so building one would mean inventing them.

    Format: Decision 'AGENTS.md is a marked region': three marker states, each with its action and reason (absent: append; present: replace between; opened but not closed: report and write nothing). Make it a three-row table.

    Format: Decision 'Re-run refreshes instructions and touches nothing else': a list giving, for each class of artifact, what extend mode does. Make it a table (Artifact / Absent / Present) with the three rows the design states. Do not add a `spec.nix` row: that rule is in task 8.1 and the delta, not in this section.

    Format: Decision 'The version gate checks; it does not write': five paragraphs reason toward a gate with distinct outcomes (declaration absent, unparseable, unchanged, backwards, advanced). Add a Mermaid flowchart with the gate nodes beside the prose, not in place of it. The prose argues the checking/judgment division, and a diagram cannot carry that.

    Format: Decision 'An ascending asset reference makes an absent store suspicious': the scope is a 2x2 (store found above or not, reference ascends or not). Make it a small table, and keep the two 'Rejected:' alternatives as a list.

    Format: Decision 'Cancellation is a fourth outcome': make it a four-row table (Outcome / Meaning), with the meanings the prose gives ('success, the document is wrong, the operation could not run', and declined). Give numeric codes only where evidence records them (operational failure 2 in current-cli-behavior.md; Cancelled 3 in first-run.md) and link those. Do not supply the document-violation code, which no file in this slice states.

    Format: Decisions 'Resolution walks upward and stops at a boundary', 'Skills are compiled in', 'spec.nix is written, because it has a consumer', and 'The closing message names the literal command per tool': short argued prose. Keep as is.

2026-08-18-conform-generated-frontmatter-names

Records version 0.1.0. This change gave the `name:` field that `htmlspec init` writes into generated skill and command frontmatter a contract: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only. Command files had been carrying the tool's invocation (`/htmlspec:apply`, `/htmlspec-apply`), and skill files conformed only by coincidence of kebab-case directory names. It moved the command name to `workflow.directory`, left `Tool::invocation` with one producer (the closing message), and added a test that reads back every generated file rather than the table the files are derived from. The risk it disproved by loading rather than by reasoning was that a loader might register a command from `name:`. Its 'one identity per workflow' clause was reversed three days later, as a regression it had introduced, by 2026-08-21-distinguish-command-names-from-skill-names.

Collapsed specification. One requirement from one capability, so there is nothing to arrange. The collapsed specification holds one requirement unit with data-change="modified". Its derivation is 'Bootstrapping installs agent instructions for the tools a project uses -> req-bootstrapping-installs-agent-instructions-for-the-tools-a-project-uses', from the full heading. No RENAMED section anywhere touches this heading. The same heading is stated in four other archived deltas (2026-08-17-project-bootstrap-cli, 2026-08-18-install-the-full-workflow-set, 2026-08-21-distinguish-command-names-from-skill-names, 2026-08-24-pass-the-description-through) and in the accepted spec, all resolving to this one identifier. Keep the source's paragraph order (eight earlier obligations, then the two new ones) and its scenario order (eight earlier, then four new).

Purpose statements. None. The one delta carries no ## Purpose, only ## MODIFIED Requirements.

Change subject. Yes. The delta restates a whole requirement whose first eight paragraphs and first eight scenarios predate this change, so a reader of the specification alone cannot tell what this change established. One sentence would cover it, drawn from tasks 5.2 and the proposal's 'What Changes'. This change added the obligations that every generated file's declared name uses only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, checked against the produced files; that the name is not the invocation, which has one producer; and that one identity serves every kind of file a workflow produces. Per-scenario change states would carry part of this in structure.

Built differs from stated. Possibly, on one point, and the reviewer should judge it. The paragraph says the name rule holds 'for each kind of file the operation writes', and scenario 'Every generated name is loadable' says 'every file it writes declares a name of lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens only'. The shared-file region (AGENTS.md) declares no name. The built test `every_generated_name_is_loadable` (crates/htmlspec-cli/src/install.rs at commit 4972234) iterates only `installed.skills` and `installed.commands`, never `installed.regions`, and its `declared_name` helper would panic on a file without `name:`. As built, the rule holds for every generated file that carries frontmatter. The accepted spec (openspec/specs/project-bootstrap/spec.md) still uses this wording today, so it is standing wording, not something the migration introduced. Otherwise the built code matches the delta. `write_commands` writes `workflow.directory`, and `Tool::invocation`'s only non-test caller is `report_next_command`. The code also goes beyond the design by removing `write_commands`'s `Tool` parameter entirely, which the delta does not address.

Evidence and verification units. There is real, citable verification, but only partial. failing-name-check-2026-08-19.md records `every_generated_name_is_loadable` failing on 21 malformed command files before the fix. That bears on 'Every generated name is loadable' and 'A malformed name is caught before release', but it records the failing run only. No evidence file records the passing run after the fix: tasks 2.5 and commit 4972234's message assert it. loading-after-rename-2026-08-19.md records regenerated command files declaring `htmlspec-*-change` identical to their skills, which bears on 'A name that is not an invocation' and 'One identity per workflow'. It also records the unchanged invocations and closing message, which bear on existing behaviour, not a scenario this change added. No source document states a verification-to-scenario link. Whether to create verification units from these records, or omit them and say so under project-migration 'A unit kind the source format has none of', is for the coordinator to decide.

2026-08-18-install-the-full-workflow-set

Records version 0.1.0. This change took `htmlspec init` from installing one workflow (`archive`) to seven, in lifecycle order: explore, new, continue, ff, apply, verify, archive. Its argument was that the hazard the old one-workflow rule guarded against is naming a command that does not exist, not shipping a workflow with no command behind it. `archive` was already agent-driven, so the old rule was narrower than the behavior it produced. The change replaced a code-comment rule and a literal-string test with a test that resolves every `htmlspec` invocation in every body against clap's own command tree. It also made the lifecycle's entry point a flag on the table, so the closing message names `new` rather than `archive`, and it modified two project-bootstrap requirements to match. Its evidence measured the install (49 files, a 36 KB shared region judged acceptable) and drove one change through the lifecycle, which found a grammar defect in the closing message that every stated test property had passed.

Collapsed specification. There is one capability and two requirements. Keep the delta's order: install, then closing message. That is also the accepted specification's relative order. No grouping is needed.

Purpose statements. None. The single delta has no `## Purpose`, so there is no non-requirement statement to account for.

Change subject. Recommended, briefly. Both requirements are MODIFIED restatements in full, so a reader of the specification alone sees the whole obligation but not what this change made of it. A short opening statement would close that gap: 'Bootstrapping previously installed a single workflow, archival. This change requires the installed instructions to cover the lifecycle from an idea to an archived change, installs a stage whether or not a command performs it, requires that no installed instruction name a command the program lacks and that this be checked mechanically, orders the workflows by the lifecycle, and makes the closing message name the lifecycle's entry point.' That wording appears in no delta, and its justification is artifact-kinds' 'A specification states the settled contract as built' (the contract read without the change) together with project-migration's allowance for a statement of the change's own subject.

Built differs from stated. Mostly consistent, with one real gap in breadth. The built check (`crates/htmlspec-cli/src/invocations.rs`, `no_shipped_body_names_an_absent_command`) resolves only the path of subcommand words. Flags, arguments, and placeholders end the path and are never checked. The test `the_withdrawn_init_path_is_not_itself_an_invocation_fault` asserts deliberately that `htmlspec init doc.html`, the withdrawn spelling the program refuses at runtime, is NOT reported. The requirement statement ('SHALL NOT name a command the program does not provide') matches what was built. The scenario 'Instructions naming an absent command' says 'an invocation the program does not provide ... the project's own checks report it', which is broader than what was built. The migrated specification should state the subcommand-level check that exists, and the coordinator should decide whether that counts as a difference to record. A lesser point: the delta scenario 'A workflow with no command behind it' says the instructions 'state that the work is the agent's'. Five new bodies open with 'This is an agent-driven operation', but `explore.md` states a stance ('You are a thinking partner') instead. That arguably satisfies the scenario and is noted only for completeness. The closing message's actual text is recorded in `evidence/seven-workflow-install-2026-08-18.md` and satisfies both requirements.

Evidence and verification units. This change does record verification that could be cited. It is not manufactured. `evidence/seven-workflow-install-2026-08-18.md` records checks that map one-to-one onto the scenarios 'Installing for a tool with commands', 'Installing for a tool without commands', 'The lifecycle is covered', 'Workflows are presented in lifecycle order', 'Generated instructions name their version', 'Naming the next command', 'Tools with different spellings', and 'The named command is the entry point'. `evidence/lifecycle-walkthrough-2026-08-18.md` records the run behind 'Instructions naming an absent command' and 'A workflow with no command behind it'. The source delta has no verification or evidence units. project-migration says to omit a unit kind the source format does not express rather than derive it 'from a source document that was not a record of them'. These evidence files are records of exactly this, so whether writing verification and evidence units that point at them counts as manufacturing is the coordinator's call. The scenarios 'Every selected tool receives something' and 'No tools selected' have no record in this change's evidence.

2026-08-21-check-release-hygiene

Records version 0.2.0. This change made release hygiene something this repository's own `scripts/check` suite enforces, as a ninth stage called `release`. It does not touch the shipped program. It exists because seven archived changes, four of which altered output a consumer relies on, had all shipped as `0.1.0` with no changelog, and no stage read the version. The change framed the check as three properties of the settled archive, not of work in progress, because a shell stage can only pass or fail. It also created the per-archive `VERSION` convention and the `CHANGELOG.md` baseline that this migration's version-carrying rule now depends on. Two sandbox-only faults came up during implementation: the new script was untracked, and the source filter excluded `VERSION`. They produced a contract paragraph that no task or evidence file in the change records.

Collapsed specification. One capability, three requirements. Keep the source order: the MODIFIED suite requirement first, because it is the umbrella that makes release hygiene a stage and binds every stage. Then 'The project records what changed in each version it ships'. Then 'An archived change records the version it shipped in'. That order also lets the archive requirement's 'the changelog SHALL carry a single baseline entry' refer back to a changelog already defined. Heading derivations: 'Project checks are runnable as one command' (first stated in 2026-08-10-html-spec, restated here and never renamed), 'The project records what changed in each version it ships', and 'An archived change records the version it shipped in'. No toolchain-packaging RENAMED section anywhere touches these three headings.

Purpose statements. None. The single delta carries no ## Purpose.

Change subject. Probably yes, briefly. The MODIFIED requirement restates the whole suite contract, and data-change="modified" on the unit cannot show that this change added four of its five paragraphs and three of its six scenarios. The source delta had the same limitation, so nothing is lost. Nothing in the delta says what the change did as a whole. A subject statement would say that the repository's own check suite, not the shipped program, gained a `release` stage asking three questions of the archive; that the seven prior archives were recorded honestly at a `0.1.0` baseline; and that the one-command requirement gained constraints binding every stage. The coordinator decides.

Built differs from stated. One narrow point. The built `scripts/check-release` (rule 3) also requires a CHANGELOG.md heading for the version Cargo.toml currently declares, not only for versions archives record: `wanted.add(declared)`. The design's Goals state this ('fails when the current version has no changelog entry'). The delta states only 'one entry per version it has shipped' and frames every rule as a property of the archive. A declared-but-unarchived version is a working-tree fact, so the built check can fail on work in progress if the version is bumped before the entry is written. That is in tension with the MODIFIED requirement's settled-record paragraph. Everything else in the delta matches what was built: the widened `srcFilter` with `isVersion`, `patchShebangs` naming the new script, the `release` stage placed last, distinctness skipped at or below `BASELINE = (0, 1, 0)`, and fault messages naming the archive and version.

Evidence and verification units. This change does record verification that could be cited. evidence/failing-check-2026-08-21.md and evidence/each-rule-observed-failing-2026-08-21.md are real run transcripts with exit statuses. Together they cover the scenarios 'An archive with no recorded version', 'A version with no entry' and 'Two archives claiming one version'. No recorded run covers 'The baseline', 'The baseline retires', 'An entry's contents', 'A reconstructed entry', or any of the MODIFIED requirement's scenarios. The sandbox run behind 'A file the source filter excludes' exists only in commit 41310f8's message and the CHANGELOG 0.2.0 entry. Whether to emit verification or evidence units that reference the two files, or to omit them and record the omission under 'A unit kind the source format has none of', is the coordinator's decision. The records exist, so any such unit would cite a record rather than invent one.

Decided. Decision 4, "Where this plan goes, and what the next change must do", as amended on 2026-10-13: the first change made in html-spec form points `scripts/check-release` at `htmlspec/`. Confirmed that at 139b206 it still reads `root / "openspec" / ADOPTION_FILE` (line 454) and `root / "openspec" / "changes" / "archive"` (line 638). The reader asked: `scripts/check-release` hardcodes `root / "openspec" / "changes" / "archive"` (line 638) and `root / "openspec" / ADOPTION_FILE` (line 454). After migration the archives' `VERSION` files live under `htmlspec/changes/archive/`. While the source survives, the `release` stage keeps checking `openspec/` and cannot see a migrated archive. Once `openspec/` is removed it exits 2 with 'no archived changes'. The accepted requirement 'An archived change records the version it shipped in' requires a form 'the project's own suite can read'. Moving the script is not a document migration, but no one else may notice it.

2026-08-21-distinguish-command-names-from-skill-names

Records version 0.1.0. This change repaired a regression the previous change (2026-08-18-conform-generated-frontmatter-names) introduced. That change set each command file's `name:` to the skill file's value, so Claude Code, Cursor and Pi each listed every workflow twice (a Pi session load showed fourteen entries for seven workflows). The fix stopped command files from declaring any name, because the file path already determines the invocation. It added a per-tool distinctness test, watched failing on 21 files before the fix. It also withdrew from project-bootstrap the scenario 'One identity per workflow', which had required the duplication, and this was the project's first withdrawal from an accepted specification. The change was needed because the contract itself asserted the defect, so a green suite could not see it; its substance is that withdrawal, which the OpenSpec delta can express only by leaving the scenario out.

Collapsed specification. One capability and one requirement, so no grouping is needed. The requirement 'Bootstrapping installs agent instructions for the tools a project uses' should be marked modified, with its 11 paragraphs in source order and its 13 scenarios in source order. The two new scenarios sit between 'A name that is not an invocation' and 'A malformed name is caught before release', exactly where the withdrawn scenario stood. If the withdrawn scenario is carried as removed (see open_questions), its place is the same slot, immediately before 'A workflow is listed once per tool'.

Purpose statements. None. The only delta, specs/project-bootstrap/spec.md, carries no ## Purpose; it opens directly with ## MODIFIED Requirements.

Change subject. Yes. The delta restates an 11-paragraph, 13-scenario requirement in full, so a reader of the specification alone (artifact-kinds 'A specification states the settled contract as built', scenario 'The contract read without the change') cannot tell which three things this change did. Scenario-level data-change can show the two added scenarios. The amended clause in paragraph 10 and the new paragraph 11 are prose inside one requirement and have no unit to carry a state, and the withdrawal is invisible because the delta simply omits the scenario. The statement would say: this change withdrew the scenario requiring a workflow's skill file and command file to declare the same name; it required instead that no two files one tool loads declare one name, and that a file needing no name to be found (a command file) declare none; it removed from the requirement's prose the clause that the same identity is used for every kind of file.

Built differs from stated. Two scenarios the delta restated unchanged disagree with what this change built. (1) 'Every generated name is loadable': its THEN says 'every file it writes declares a name of lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens only'. As built, command files (and the AGENTS.md region) declare no name. The test `every_generated_name_is_loadable` (crates/htmlspec-cli/src/install.rs) skips any file without `name:` and asserts exactly 28 declared names, one per workflow per tool that receives skills (evidence/failing-distinctness-check-2026-08-20.md records 49 before the fix and 28 after). What was built is that every declared name is well-formed, not that every file declares one. (2) 'A name that is not an invocation': its THEN says a generated command file's 'declared name identifies the workflow', but a generated command file now declares no name, so the scenario is vacuous as built. Paragraph 9's 'This SHALL hold for each kind of file the operation writes' is likewise vacuous for command files. Task 5.4 deliberately kept these intact, and today's accepted openspec/specs/project-bootstrap/spec.md (lines 232–238) still carries both unchanged. Separately, paragraph 11's claim that a command file is a kind 'whose invocation is determined by its file path' was verified by loading for Claude Code and Pi only. Cursor also receives no name, and its loader was never exercised (task 4.5, evidence loading-after-omission). That is a risk the design accepted, not a divergence, but it bounds what any verification unit may claim.

Evidence and verification units. This change does hold genuine records that could back evidence units, so the omission is not forced here. evidence/failing-distinctness-check-2026-08-20.md records the check watched failing (it backs 'A repeated name is caught before release'). evidence/loading-after-omission-2026-08-20.md, section 'The load, observed 2026-08-21', records the session load (it backs 'A workflow is listed once per tool', and the invocations being unchanged). Both are real records, not documents rewritten into records. Verification units would be different: the tests `no_tool_receives_a_name_twice` and `every_generated_name_is_loadable` exist in the code, but no source document is a verification record keyed to scenarios, so building verification units would mean deriving them. Whatever is chosen must not claim Cursor as verified (task 4.5), and must not claim 'Every generated name is loadable' was verified for command files, because that test reads only skill files.

The reader asked: Carrying the withdrawn scenario. The destination can express what OpenSpec's MODIFIED convention could only omit: a unit with data-change="removed" kept present 'so reviewers can see what is being withdrawn' (document-schema 'Semantic units declare a change state', scenario 'Requirement being withdrawn', stated for requirements; this requirement says every semantic unit carries a state). The withdrawn scenario's text is in this change's proposal and evidence, not in its delta. Carrying it would put text in the specification that the delta does not contain, which project-migration's collapse requirement allows only where migration can say why it was needed. No requirement decides whether migration should restore it from the proposal, derive per-scenario states by diffing against the previous accepted spec, or leave it absent. This needs a reviewer's decision.

2026-08-22-accept-a-described-change

Records version 0.3.0. This change repaired the `new` workflow's authoring prose after an agent refused, twice, a complete description of a browser tally-counter app. The instruction demanded a need stated as a malfunction (a measurement, an error message, a behavior somebody hit), which new work cannot have. It also never let the agent derive a change name, and it overrode the correct inference the agent had already written down. The change amended new.md and ff.md so a need may be an absence of capability with its own three-part concrete form, and so the agent derives and reports a name. It wrote both into artifact-kinds: a modified proposal requirement and a new 'described change' requirement. Its only agent run showed the prose landed, but no change could be created, because generated command files discarded the contributor's description. So the end-to-end task was dropped, and the defect went to 2026-08-24-pass-the-description-through (0.4.0).

Collapsed specification. One capability and two requirements, so there is no collapse problem. Keep the delta's order: the modified 'A proposal argues value and the tool does not shape it' (req-a-proposal-argues-value-and-the-tool-does-not-shape-it) first, then the added 'A described change starts without a supplied name' (req-a-described-change-starts-without-a-supplied-name). That is also the order in the accepted artifact-kinds specification, so a reader moving between the two finds them in the same place. Neither heading was ever renamed. The first identifier is shared with 2026-08-14-separate-artifact-kinds, which established the requirement, and that is correct, not a collision. The derivations file agrees on both identifiers and reports no collisions or scenario clashes for this slice.

Purpose statements. None. The single artifact-kinds delta carries no ## Purpose, so there is no non-requirement content to account for.

Change subject. Not for the collapse, since there is one delta. There is a separate question the source raises itself. Task 5.2 says 'The boundary is worth stating at archival: a prose repair to authoring guidance cannot be verified end-to-end while the invocation withholds the contributor's input', and the delta does not state it. A statement of that boundary would be text found in tasks.md but in no delta. Whether it belongs in the specification (for example beside the added requirement) is flagged, not decided.

Built differs from stated. Yes, for the ADDED requirement 'A described change starts without a supplied name'. Its scenario 'A description with no name' says the agent 'derives a name, reports it, and creates the change without a further exchange', and 'A description already carrying its scope' says the workflow does not ask again. What 0.3.0 built was guidance text that says this (amended-guidance). End to end, the built product discarded the description before any agent saw it (described-change-run: 0 matches for ARGUMENTS in the generated files, install.rs:124), so no change was created. Derivation from a contributor's own description was never observed; the name in the run was quoted from the worked example. Task 5.2 was dropped for this reason, and the 0.3.0 CHANGELOG entry says so. The behavior became reachable only at 0.4.0 (2026-08-24-pass-the-description-through), whose CHANGELOG notes '0.3.0 shipped with all 49 files missing both halves and a fully green suite.' The need-form obligations in the MODIFIED requirement match what was built. No requirement I can name decides how the migrated specification records 'built as guidance, unobservable end-to-end at this version' against scenarios that state end-to-end behavior.

Evidence and verification units. This change does record verification that could be cited, and it is transcript-based by the design's explicit decision ('Guidance is the fix, not a check': no test exists or should be added). refusal-transcript records the pre-change failure the scenario 'Guidance that demands a defect' describes. amended-guidance records the installed text that satisfies the two-form need, derive-and-report, and ask-only-for-what-is-missing statements, and says it verifies text, not behavior. described-change-run records an agent response that bears out 'A need that is an absence' (form named), the no-confirmation clause, and 'A request with no work in it' (the agent asked when no description arrived, though by accident). It explicitly does not verify 'A description with no name' or 'A description already carrying its scope'. 'A derived name a contributor rejects' has no record. The automated results (cargo test, ./scripts/check, openspec validate --all) live only in commit b995808's message and cannot be cited from the change. A specification with no verification draws the warning named in 'Intended content is guidance and enforced structure is validity', so omitting the units has a visible cost here.

With no runbooks.json or documents/*.html, nothing else is owed. The reader asked: This change holds no .openspec.yaml, no runbooks.json, and no documents/*.html, so it has no keys, predecessor declaration, or in-format documents to report.

Decided. The second review settled this on 2026-10-13 (its question 6, "Links the source did not write"): add no link the source did not write, beyond what a convention or requirement asks for. The reader asked: Task 5.2 says its follow-up was 'Filed separately' but gives no name. It is 2026-08-24-pass-the-description-through, whose proposal names this change. Neither change states a predecessor. 'A change states the change it follows' makes a predecessor a declaration the author writes, so the migrated follow-up should not gain one inferred from this link. A plain hyperlink from task 5.2's reason is a different act, and whether migration may add it is not decided by any requirement I can name.

Decided. Convention 3, "Source paths stay as text, and links go to the migrated counterpart", as amended on 2026-10-13: `openspec/specs/artifact-kinds/spec.md:36` and `:59` stay as text in the proposal and task 1.3, and each also links to the migrated requirement. There is no `data-refs`, because the words name it by path and line, not by heading. The evidence keeps them untouched. The reader asked: Historical line citations into the source's Markdown spec: `openspec/specs/artifact-kinds/spec.md:36` in the proposal and task 1.3, and `:36` and `:59` in refusal-transcript. They point at a path and line the migrated project will not hold. The evidence keeps them regardless. For the converted proposal and tasks, whether to keep them as historical text or re-point them to the requirement identifiers (req-intended-content-is-guidance-and-enforced-structure-is-validity; req-a-proposal-argues-value-and-the-tool-does-not-shape-it) is silent in the contract.

Decided. Decision 5, "Where a change built something other than it stated", as amended on 2026-10-13: the archived specification records what the change built, with a note naming the deviation. The added requirement was built as guidance, and its scenarios could not be observed through the 0.3.0 command surface until 2026-08-24-pass-the-description-through passed the description through. The reader asked: The end-to-end gap above: the added requirement's scenarios state behavior the 0.3.0 product could not exhibit. 'the implemented result SHALL be what the migrated specification records' applies, but nothing says how to express 'the obligation was built as guidance and was unobservable until a later change' in a specification unit. Decide centrally.

2026-08-24-pass-the-description-through

Records version 0.4.0. The change found that being 'asked for what you already said' had a second, mechanical cause below the prose accept-a-described-change had fixed. No generated skill or command declared an `argument-hint` or carried `$ARGUMENTS`, so all seven workflows, on every tool with a command surface, discarded what a contributor typed: 49 files, all passing a green 0.3.0 suite. It made each workflow's input a row in `WORKFLOWS`, emitted it from both writers, opened every body with a 'What you were asked' section that tells an empty input from a lost one, and checked both halves against the files an install produces. A live Pi run then turned the recorded tally-mark description into a change on the first exchange. The contract is four paragraphs and five scenarios added to project-bootstrap's single install requirement, released as 0.4.0. The bare-invocation case was never observed live, and its task is dropped with a stated reason.

Collapsed specification. One requirement, so there is no grouping to decide. Keep the requirement with its 15 statement paragraphs and 18 scenarios in the source's order: the new paragraphs sit 9 to 12, between 'Instructions SHALL record the version...' and the generated-name paragraphs, and the new scenarios sit 9 to 13, between 'Generated instructions name their version' and 'Every generated name is loadable'. The heading was never renamed. It is stated identically in 2026-08-17-project-bootstrap-cli, both 2026-08-18 changes, 2026-08-21-distinguish-command-names-from-skill-names, and here, and no project-bootstrap delta has a RENAMED section. So it derives req-bootstrapping-installs-agent-instructions-for-the-tools-a-project-uses from the full heading, the same identifier in each of those archived specifications. The 18 scenario headings are distinct, so there is no collision within this document.

Purpose statements. None. The one delta has no ## Purpose; it opens directly at ## MODIFIED Requirements.

Change subject. Yes. With one modified requirement of 15 paragraphs, a reader of the specification alone cannot tell which obligation this change established: data-change='modified' says the requirement changed, not what changed. Marking scenarios added or unchanged covers the five new scenarios but not the four new paragraphs, which are not units. The statement would say that this change added four obligations to the bootstrap requirement, and that the rest of the requirement is carried unchanged from 2026-08-21. The four are: text typed after a workflow's invocation reaches the agent, only for kinds of file a tool invokes (so not a shared file like the AGENTS.md region); each workflow declares its own input; a bare invocation stays valid, and an absent argument reads as absent rather than lost; and the declaration and the placeholder are both checked in the files an install produces.

Built differs from stated. None against the delta. The design's single shared sentence for an empty input is not what shipped, but the delta defers to 'the workflow's own guidance on a missing input', and that is what shipped: new, ff, and explore ask, while apply, verify, continue, and archive infer the change and name it. The hints shipped as '[the idea or question to think through]', '[a description of the work]' for both new and ff, and '[the change to <verb>, or nothing to infer it]' for the other four. That satisfies 'A workflow declares what it takes', because new and ff take the same input. One scenario was not observed after building: 'An invocation carrying nothing', whose task 6.4 was dropped. The build enforces it only structurally, through the optional-form assertion in the table-level test and the sentence about emptiness in each body. That leaves the scenario unverified; it does not make the build differ.

Evidence and verification units. Verification exists and can be cited for three of the five new scenarios. 'A dropped argument is caught before release' has the-checks-failing (both checks failing on the unrepaired tree, 49 plus 49). 'A delivery kind with no invocation' has the-checks-failing (AGENTS.md absent from the file-level output, by construction). 'An invocation carrying a description' has pi-substitutes (the live Pi run). the-loss is evidence of the defect, not verification of the built behavior. Nothing verifies 'An invocation carrying nothing' (6.4 dropped, no run) or 'A workflow declares what it takes', since no check compares hints across workflows and the per-workflow table field makes it structural only. The checks passing after the repair (task 5.5, and 'All 9 suite stages pass at 0.4.0' in commit 4f2f3e7's message) are recorded only in a ticked task and a commit message, not in an evidence file. The 13 unchanged scenarios have no verification in this change.

2026-08-24-report-in-the-contributors-terms

Records version 0.5.0. This change founded workflow-reporting, the first contract to govern what a workflow says to the contributor at its end. A contributor who described a tally app got three good documents and a report made of a task order, a warning count, and two questions they never raised. The change argues that the report was obedient rather than careless: every one of the seven instruction bodies' report sections was written about artifacts, and apply.md was worse than the new.md that produced the complaint. It states three obligations once. A report leads with a fact in the contributor's vocabulary, quotes prose the artifacts already hold, and names the boundary where nothing runs yet. It glosses every pointer, bounded by the deletion test. It settles what the agent can settle. No program check can see a report's register, so the change is verified by four transcripts: the failing report, then new, apply, and archive runs after the repair. Each transcript states what it does not establish.

Collapsed specification. One capability, three requirements, all added. Keep the delta's order: register ('A report answers the contributor in their own terms'), then pointers ('A report names what its references point at'), then settling ('An agent settles what it can and reports the decision'). That order follows the proposal's 'What Changes' bullets and the dependency between them: a report must first be about the right thing before its references and its open questions matter. With a single capability, no per-capability grouping is needed.

Purpose statements. None. The one delta has no ## Purpose. The accepted openspec/specs/workflow-reporting/spec.md does carry an author-written Purpose ('Defines what a workflow owes the contributor who invoked it... A report is not an artifact... seven workflows each writing their own report guidance is what this exists to prevent'). It was written in this change's own archival commit (bfc3835), but it is outside this change directory and so outside this slice's entities.

Change subject. Yes, briefly. The capability's name appears only in the delta's directory path (specs/workflow-reporting/), which the collapse drops, and nothing in the delta says the capability is new or that no requirement governed a report before. A reader of the specification alone could not tell that this change founded the capability ('The contract read without the change'). It would say: this change founds the workflow-reporting capability. Before it, no accepted requirement reached a workflow's closing report, and each of the seven instruction bodies carried its own report guidance. The change states three obligations every workflow's report owes. The accepted spec's Purpose, written at this change's archival, is the author's own wording for most of this, if the coordinator decides it may be drawn on.

Built differs from stated. Not in the delta. Its three requirements are byte-identical to the accepted workflow-reporting spec, and the built bodies carry the obligations. The built result does differ from the design and tasks in one respect the delta says nothing about. The pointer rule is repeated verbatim in all seven instruction bodies, because each body must be self-contained, and a second test pins that wording: `the_pointer_rule_is_worded_the_same_everywhere` in crates/htmlspec-assets/src/instructions.rs, alongside `every_workflow_says_what_to_report`. The design said the bodies would 'conform to one statement rather than restating it seven ways', and tasks.md names only the section-presence test. This is recorded in commit bfc3835 and CHANGELOG 0.5.0 ('Two checks... Both were observed failing first'), not in the change's documents. The migrated specification's requirements need no change for it.

Evidence and verification units. This change's evidence does record verification that could be cited, and it is a record of verification, not a document being mined for it. Per requirement: 'A report answers the contributor in their own terms' is checked in the-report-received-after (new: first claim, surfacing, boundary, artifact facts at the close) and the-archive-report (archive: first claim, facts as annotation). the-apply-report explicitly does not establish the opening line. 'A report names what its references point at' is checked in the-report-received-after (5/5), the-apply-report (5/5 plus check counts with kinds), and the-archive-report (warnings with kinds), with the-report-received as the failing baseline. 'An agent settles what it can and reports the decision' is checked in the-report-received-after and the-apply-report. Each transcript states its own limit: lighter load, missing opening, a miscount. Each also states that the register obligation's acceptance is the contributor's reading, not a check (task 4.3). The two Rust tests verify the instruction bodies, not reports, and no evidence file records their runs. Whether to produce evidence and verification units from these records, or to omit them and record the omission, is the coordinator's decision. The records exist, so omitting them would be a choice, not a necessity.

2026-08-30-finish-the-archival

Records version 0.6.0. This change made `htmlspec archive` perform the operation it is named for. Before it, the command validated a change's specification, printed that archival 'may proceed', exited zero, and left the change in `changes/`. Its one gate, the version check, had never fired, because it looked for versions in archive directory names that nothing ever wrote. To let the program write, the change withdrew project-bootstrap's sentence 'a command whose stated job is checking SHALL NOT write to the project it checks' and kept its real content: archival never touches the declaration. It then specified archival as atomic and date-named, refusing on the contract and asking about the work, checking whether the merge happened by comparing identifiers without performing it, and offering `--check`. It also added `list`, `status`, `instructions` and `store` under OpenSpec's names. It is the change where the program began writing to the project. Its four evidence files are what justify the withdrawal and the new commands.

Collapsed specification. Suggested; the arrangement is the agent's to choose under 'A change's delta specifications collapse into that change's one specification'. Use one group per capability, because the contract is applied to accepted specifications one capability at a time, and a reader checking what reached which capability needs that boundary. Put project-bootstrap first: its one requirement is the version gate, which archival checks before anything else and which 'Archival refuses on the contract…' lists as its first refusing condition. Within toolchain-packaging, replace the source's MODIFIED/ADDED split, now redundant because state sits on each unit, with two subgroups in source order. (a) Archival: 'Archival produces the specification and updates the accepted contract', 'Archival refuses on the contract and asks about the work', 'Archival assesses the merge and never performs it', 'An archived change is named for its date and refuses to collide', 'Archival is drivable without a person present', 'Archival supports a mode that checks without performing'. (b) The command surface: 'The command surface names its operations as OpenSpec names them', 'The command surface reports what a project holds', 'The command surface reports a change's completion', 'The workflow instructions are available from the command surface', 'Specifications can live in a repository other than the one being worked on'.

Purpose statements. Neither delta has a '## Purpose'. The project-bootstrap delta is one '## MODIFIED Requirements' section (1 requirement, 10 scenarios). The toolchain-packaging delta has '## MODIFIED' (2 requirements), '## ADDED' (9) and '## RENAMED' (1 pair, no prose), with 49 scenarios in all. The only content that is not a requirement is the RENAMED pair, which becomes a `renamed-from` paragraph.

Change subject. Yes. Neither delta has a Purpose, and neither says what the change did; only project-bootstrap's last paragraph hints at it. A specification read alone would show twelve requirements across two capabilities and not the one defect that joins them. Suggested text: 'This change made `htmlspec archive` perform the archival it is named for. Before it, the command checked a change's specification, reported that archival may proceed, and left the change where it was, while its version gate compared every declaration against 0.0.0 because it looked for versions in directory names. Archival now moves the change into the archive, names it for the date, and records the declared version, completing or leaving the project untouched. It reads the last archived version from each archived change's recorded version. It refuses on the contract, asks about the work, and checks whether the merge happened without performing it. The change adds a check-only mode and four commands, list, status, instructions and store, under OpenSpec's names, and narrows project-bootstrap's check-only sentence to a reservation on the act.' That text appears in no delta, and the reason is the one the collapse requirement gives: a specification must let a reader tell what its change established without reading the change's other documents.

Built differs from stated. (1) 'Specifications can live in a repository other than the one being worked on' requires the operations that read and write specifications and changes to be able to act on a registered project, and forbids falling back to the working directory. At cf11132, `--store` is a global clap flag, so every subcommand accepts it, but `main.rs` passes it only to `list` and `status`. `archive`, `validate`, `format` and `new` resolve the working directory's project (`archive` calls `ProjectRoot::resolve(Path::new("."))`). So `htmlspec archive --store far` archives the local change: exactly the silent fallback the requirement forbids. Task 7.3 ('Add the selection flag to the operations that read and write…') is checked, but every store test drives `list`. The current tree passes `--store` to more commands (run, preflight, sync), but still not to archive, validate or new. (2) 'Archival supports a mode that checks without performing' says the mode fails 'exactly where archival would refuse', but lists only four conditions: version, presence, kind, validation. The collision refusal required by 'An archived change is named for its date and refuses to collide' is in `perform`, which runs only after check mode has already returned success. So `archive --check` reports 'ready' for a change whose target archive already exists, and `archive` then refuses it. What was built matches the list of four, not the word 'exactly'. The gap is still there today: check mode returns at commands.rs:1370, and the collision check is at :3766. (3) Built with no requirement stating it. `archive` with no argument selects the only active change and announces it, or lists several (task 5.5, test `archival_with_no_argument_selects_or_asks`). A VERSION write that fails after the move reports the change as archived and exits nonzero (design decision 'The move is atomic…', task 4.5). No delta states either behaviour. The collapse requirement says the migrated specification records what was built. For (1) and (2), recording what was built would write a defect into the contract as a SHALL, so each needs a person's decision rather than a mechanical application of that rule.

Evidence and verification units. Omit both evidence and verification units: nothing in this change's documents records verification of the built result. The four evidence files record the state before the change: the gate defect, the command counts, the search for write rules, and what OpenSpec's workflow does. They support why requirements exist, not that the requirements hold. The tasks record verification only as 56 checked boxes, and one of them (4.9) names a test. At cf11132, `crates/htmlspec-cli/tests/archive.rs` holds tests matching most 'Assert…' tasks, for example `an_occupied_archive_target_is_refused`, `check_mode_fails_where_archival_refuses`, `status_and_archival_agree_about_open_tasks`, `emitted_instructions_are_the_installed_instructions`, `a_store_whose_project_is_gone_does_not_fall_back` and `the_command_surface_uses_openspecs_names`, and a unit test `a_declined_offer_stops` covers the declined offer. Code is not a source document of this change, though, so deriving verification units from it would create a record. The coverage is also not what the tasks claim: 4.12's plain 'ready' case has no test. If evidence units were wanted, the files map to requirements as follows: the-version-gate-never-fired backs 'Archival requires the project version to advance' (the recorded-version paragraph) and 'Archival produces…' (the completion paragraph); the-write-restriction-search backs 'Archival supports a mode that checks without performing' and the project-bootstrap reservation paragraph; what-openspec-archival-does backs 'Archival assesses the merge and never performs it'; the-command-usage-measured backs 'The command surface names its operations…' and 'The command surface reports what a project holds'. No requirement decides whether a record made before the change can serve as a specification's evidence unit or only as a link.
