2026-08-31-sync-a-change-into-the-accepted-contract

Records version 0.7.0. This change gave the merge that archival names, but is forbidden to perform, a place to live. It added `htmlspec sync`, a read-only report of which requirement identifiers a change's specification states, which the accepted specifications already hold, and which are absent. Sync is computed by the same function archival calls (shipped as `merge_state`). The change also added an eighth workflow stage that carries the agent's half of the merge. It was needed because archival's note told contributors to "apply the change's contract" when no command did so. It was also needed because toolchain-packaging's rule that an operation OpenSpec provides keeps OpenSpec's name had no `sync` in its fixed spelling list. The load-bearing choices are that sync never writes an accepted specification, and that it succeeds while requirements are absent, refusing only when the comparison would mean nothing.

Collapsed specification. There is one capability and three requirements, so no grouping is needed. Keep the source order: the reporting operation, then the workflow stage, then the modified naming requirement. The stage requirement's 'the requirement above' is a positional reference to the operation requirement. The operation requirement must precede it unless that phrase becomes an identifier link.

Purpose statements. None. The only delta, toolchain-packaging, carries no ## Purpose, so nothing of that kind needs accounting for.

Change subject. Yes, briefly. The two added requirements describe themselves. The modified naming requirement is restated in full, and nothing in the delta says that its only change is `sync` in the spelling list, so a reader of the specification alone cannot tell what this change did to it. A statement would say: 'This change adds `sync`, a read-only report of which of a change's requirement identifiers have reached the accepted specifications, computed by the comparison archival uses. It adds a workflow stage carrying the agent's half of the merge, and adds `sync` to the fixed spellings, which is the only change to "The command surface names its operations as OpenSpec names them".' This is text with no source counterpart. The reason it is needed is project-migration's 'A change's delta specifications collapse into that change's one specification', together with artifact-kinds' 'The contract read without the change'.

Built differs from stated. Nothing I found shows the built program differing from what the delta states. Commit ee4301c added `merge_state`, the `sync` subcommand, and four tests: the_comparison_partitions_what_the_change_states, archival_and_sync_name_the_same_absent_requirements, a_change_stating_no_identifiers_has_nothing_absent, and sync_does_not_write_the_accepted_specifications. Three differences are outside the delta: (1) the design and task 3.1 name the function `unmerged_requirements`, and it shipped renamed `merge_state` (CHANGELOG 0.7.0), which is naming only; (2) the stage was never installed into this repository's committed skill copies (see the tasks entity), while the delta's obligation is about what bootstrapping installs, which the compiled table satisfies; (3) the accepted text has since gained a fourth set from a later change, which must not be imported. Answer: null.

Evidence and verification units. Verification: omit, and record why. No evidence file records a check. All four are pre-implementation findings from tasks 1.1–1.4. Tasks 3.3, 4.6, and 6.1–6.3 claim checks were run but record no output. The four tests in ee4301c are never named in the change's documents; CHANGELOG 0.7.0 names one. Building verification units from the code or the changelog would derive a record from sources that are not this change's record. Evidence: the four files exist and could back evidence units. 2026-09-02-carry-task-progress-into-the-listing

Records version 0.8.0. Before this change, `htmlspec list` printed only change names. The accepted requirement that created it says the enumeration exists so a workflow can select what it acts on, and names gave nothing to select on. This change made each active change carry its completion as a count per task state. The counts come from the single counter that `status` and archival already share, so the three operations cannot disagree. A change with no tasks document shows its completion as absent, not zero. Partway through implementation the scope grew: archival now reports an unmerged contract as an unsynced change, names `htmlspec sync --change <name>`, rewords its question, and carries `needsSync` in its payload. That addition is recorded only in tasks section 6, one evidence file, and the second modified requirement. The proposal and design never mention it.

Collapsed specification. One capability, so one group, holding its two requirements in source order. First 'The command surface reports what a project holds', the change's subject (tasks 1 to 5). Second 'Archival assesses the merge and never performs it', the mid-implementation addition (tasks 6). Both are data-change="modified". With no Purpose to introduce the group, it should say which accepted specification the two requirements modify (toolchain-packaging). Derivations: 'The command surface reports what a project holds' -> req-the-command-surface-reports-what-a-project-holds, and 'Archival assesses the merge and never performs it' -> req-archival-assesses-the-merge-and-never-performs-it. Neither was ever the target of a RENAMED section.

Purpose statements. None. The only delta (toolchain-packaging) holds '## MODIFIED Requirements' alone and has no '## Purpose'.

Change subject. Yes, one short statement. The delta has no Purpose, and read alone its two requirements look unrelated: one is about listing, the other about archival. What connects them appears only in task 6.1, the evidence, and CHANGELOG 0.8.0: each repairs a report by reusing a computation the program already makes (the task counter; merge_state) instead of recomputing it. Suggested wording: 'This change made the enumeration of active changes carry each change's completion as a count per task state, drawn from the same counter the completion report and archival use, and made archival report a change whose contract has not reached the accepted specifications as unsynced, naming the sync operation as it is invoked.'

Built differs from stated. Three places. (1) The delta counts apart 'a task that declares no state'. The built `Completion.undeclared` (commit 9af58cf) also counts a task that declares a state outside the vocabulary, according to its doc comment and its `_ =>` match arm. So the built behavior is broader than the delta, which is silent on out-of-vocabulary states. (2) The scenario 'The enumeration and the completion report agree' says 'any active change … the two report the same counts'. For a change with no tasks document, `status` reports total=0 while the listing omits the counts. evidence/the-listing-agrees-with-status-2026-09-01.md records this as a deliberate difference in what each can express, and prove-listing.py scores it as agreement. So as built, the scenario holds only for changes that have a tasks document. (3) Built and tested but stated by no requirement: the denominator counts dropped tasks (design, task 4.3, a test); a three-valued overall state (todo, in-progress, done) in the report and in payload `state`; column alignment; the literal `no tasks`; and the payload field names (name, state, total, tasks{todo,inProgress,done,dropped,undeclared}). These are silences, not contradictions. Adding them as obligations would be a decision nothing in the source took. The archival requirement matches the built wording recorded in evidence. No difference was found there.

Evidence and verification units. The source delta holds no evidence or verification units, but this change's evidence does record citable verification. evidence/the-listing-agrees-with-status-2026-09-01.md, with evidence/prove-listing.py, verifies these scenarios by numeric comparison: 'A change's progress is visible in the listing', 'Outstanding work that was abandoned' (gamma), 'The enumeration and the completion report agree' (5/5), 'A change with no tasks document' (epsilon), and 'Order does not follow progress' (name order). evidence/archival-names-the-sync-it-checked-2026-09-01.md records a real-project run: the warning appears when unsynced, clears once the contract is applied, and agrees with `htmlspec sync`. It also lists the tests that pin 'A change whose contract has not been synced', 'The question asked about an unsynced change', 'A change whose contract was applied', and 'An agent reads the condition rather than inferring it'. No evidence file covers 'Two changes at the same fraction in different states' (the scratch run has no all-in-progress change) or 'A task that declares no state'. Only code tests (`the_same_fraction_in_two_states_is_distinguishable`, `each_state_is_counted_apart`) cover them, and no evidence records those tests. Whether verification units written from these records count as 'manufactured' under the delta-collapse requirement is for the coordinator.

Decided. Convention 2, "Records are carried as written, and so is disagreement with them": the proposal and design cross as written, covering only the listing, and do not take on the archival/sync work. That work stays where the source recorded it, in tasks section 6 and the second modified requirement. Under convention 6, evidence/archival-names-the-sync-it-checked-2026-09-01.md, its only record of reasoning, may back an evidence unit for that requirement in the specification. The reader asked: Scope is split across documents. The proposal and design cover only the listing. The archival/sync work lives only in tasks section 6, one evidence file, and the second modified requirement. The migrated proposal and design should not gain it. The migrated tasks section 6 and the specification should link evidence/archival-names-the-sync-it-checked-2026-09-01.md, which holds that work's only reasoning, including two rejected alternatives.

2026-09-02-state-a-changes-place-in-a-sequence

Records version 0.9.0. This change (0.9.0) gave a change a way to state the one change it follows. Before it, nothing in the project related one change to another, so a sequence whose order was the whole argument (a contract written before the work it grades) could be archived out of order while every artifact validated. It resolves the stated name across the archive in three distinct ways (archived by matching with the date prefix removed, active, or unmatched), reports cycles as contradictions, and has archival report an unresolved predecessor as a question rather than a refusal. The listing carries the same fact without changing its order. The design put the declaration in `.openspec.yaml`. During implementation the evidence found that an html-spec change has no such file, and the declaration was built as a `FOLLOWS` file instead. The delta's wording is deliberately silent on which file holds it.

Collapsed specification. One group per capability, artifact-kinds first: 'A change states the change it follows' (added), 'A stated predecessor is resolved across the archive' (added), 'Archival produces the specification and then updates the accepted contract' (modified), then toolchain-packaging's 'The command surface reports what a project holds' (modified). Capability order and reading order coincide here: what is declared, how it resolves, then the two operations that report it (archival, then the listing). Nothing needs reordering. Each group needs a capability label, since neither delta has a Purpose to introduce it.

Purpose statements. Neither delta carries a ## Purpose. artifact-kinds opens with ## ADDED Requirements and toolchain-packaging with ## MODIFIED Requirements.

Change subject. Yes. Two deltas, no Purpose, and neither says what the change did as a whole. It would say: a change may state the one change it follows, declared beside its documents and never inferred. The program resolves the stated name across the archive to archived (with the date removed), active or unmatched, and treats a cycle as a contradiction. Archival reports an unresolved predecessor as a finding it asks about and never refuses, and the listing carries the predecessor beside each change without changing its order. Whether this statement may name the `FOLLOWS` file is an open question (below).

Built differs from stated. The delta itself does not disagree with what was built, because it deliberately does not name the file. The design, the proposal and task 3.1 placed the declaration in `.openspec.yaml`, and what was built is a `FOLLOWS` file in the change directory (evidence/where-the-declaration-goes-2026-09-02.md). The CHANGELOG 0.9.0 entry names `FOLLOWS`. The built result also goes beyond the delta's text in three places, without contradicting it. First, archival carries a cycle as the payload value `followsCycle` and calls it a contradiction, while the modified archival requirement speaks only of an unarchived predecessor. Cycles are covered generally by 'A stated predecessor is resolved across the archive'. Second, the listing carries the three-way `follows.resolution` as well as the `follows.resolved` boolean the delta asks for, plus a top-level `followsCycles`. Third, archival's payload states `outOfOrder` alongside `unresolvedPredecessor`. One more qualification, not a disagreement: the delta's reason for one predecessor ('One relation is what the observed need requires') sits beside evidence showing that the motivating fourth change has three predecessors, and only one of them is expressible.

Evidence and verification units. Verification exists and could be cited. evidence/the-sequence-against-real-projects-2026-09-02.md, produced by evidence/prove-sequence.py, records 31 passing assertions against the built binary. They cover these scenarios: 'A predecessor that has been archived' (5.2), 'A predecessor still being worked on' (5.1), 'A predecessor that no longer exists under that name' (5.3), 'Two changes that each follow the other' (5.4), 'A change archived after its predecessor' (5.2), 'A change archived before its predecessor' (5.1, including `--yes`), 'An agent archiving out of order' (5.1 and 5.5, payload), 'A change whose predecessor is unfinished' (5.5, listing) and 'Order does not follow the stated sequence' (5.4). No carried record verifies 'A change whose predecessor is done' (listing), 'An ordering is never derived', or 'A change that follows nothing' as stated (validation succeeds): 5.5 checks only that the listing's `follows` is absent for the contract. Whether evidence and verification units are made from these records is a central decision. I report only that the records exist and what they cover.

Mapped. project-migration's "A source change's own configuration is surveyed, and its predecessor becomes its declaration", with artifact-kinds' "A change states the change it follows": the survey at 139b206 reports follows for 2026-09-26-carry-a-runbook-to-another-machine (log-a-runbook-run), 2026-09-26-log-a-runbook-run (establish-a-runbook) and 2026-09-29-keep-evidence-out-of-document-discovery (migrate-an-openspec-project). Each value is written to FOLLOWS exactly as the source wrote it, and each file also crosses byte-identical under decision 1. This change states none, so it has no FOLLOWS. The reader asked: Cross-slice: this change built the `FOLLOWS` file, html-spec's per-change predecessor declaration (crates/htmlspec-cli/src/project.rs:81). Three later changes record a predecessor as a `follows:` key in `.openspec.yaml`: 2026-09-26-carry-a-runbook-to-another-machine (follows log-a-runbook-run), 2026-09-26-log-a-runbook-run (follows establish-a-runbook) and 2026-09-29-keep-evidence-out-of-document-discovery (follows migrate-an-openspec-project). 2026-09-26-log-a-runbook-run/proposal.md says why: `FOLLOWS` files break the OpenSpec mirror's file classification. The destination can express that fact, since 'A change states the change it follows' requires the declaration to live with the change's whole-directory facts. But the project-migration contract has no row mapping a `.openspec.yaml` `follows:` key to anything, and the accepted contract deliberately does not name `FOLLOWS`. The central `.openspec.yaml` decision needs to say whether those values become `FOLLOWS` files in the migrated archives or are dropped with a reason. This slice's own `.openspec.yaml` has no `follows` key.

Open. Whether this change's migrated specification, in its summary or a requirement, may name the FOLLOWS file. At 139b206 artifact-kinds' "A change states the change it follows" still says only that the declaration lives with the change's whole-directory facts, while project-migration's configuration requirement now names FOLLOWS as a migration's target. The built FOLLOWS file satisfies the delta's wording, so decision 5 finds no deviation to note. No decision or convention settles whether naming the file records what was built or adds an obligation the author withheld.

Decided. Convention 3, "Source paths stay as text, and links go to the migrated counterpart": paths inside evidence are untouched, so the pre-archive paths and the commit 595e38c stay as historical citations.   • design.md

    Does: Takes the six decisions that turn 'this change follows that one' into something a program can check. The successor declares it, because the predecessor cannot know its successors' names. It sits in the per-change declaration, because a reference addresses a unit and a change is not one. It is matched against the archive with the date prefix removed, because equality fails exactly when the predecessor is done. Archival reports it and does not refuse, because abandoned sequences must stay archivable. The listing carries it without reordering. A cycle is reported and not resolved. It also rules out inference from names, dates, or requirement identifiers, and a general dependency graph. One of these decisions, the file location, was overturned during implementation.

    source: openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-02-state-a-changes-place-in-a-sequence/design.md

    destination: htmlspec/changes/archive/2026-09-02-state-a-changes-place-in-a-sequence/design.html

    disposition: converted

Make each a decision unit (document-schema 'A decision records its outcome and rationale') and keep the rejected alternative in its rationale.

    Format: 'Rejected: inferring the sequence' and 'Rejected: a general dependency graph' are decisions stated in the negative. Make them decision units whose outcome is the refusal.

    Format: 'Resolving a predecessor across the archive boundary': the three-row table (in the archive / active / nowhere | meaning | what archival says) is already the right shape. Keep it as is. Do not also draw it as a diagram.

    Format: 'Rejected: inferring the sequence' has three bold-led paragraphs (From names / From creation dates / From requirement identifiers), each giving one reason and in two cases citing the accepted sentence it would falsify. Make it a three-row table (inferred from | why refused).

    Format: 'Why archival reports and does not refuse': the path of report, then ask, then `--yes` answers in advance is one sentence. Keep it as prose. The fuller three-way table (--check / no terminal / --yes) is already in the evidence, so link to it rather than redrawing it.

    Format: 'A cycle is reported and never resolved': the bounded walk over predecessors takes two sentences. Keep it as prose; a diagram would add nothing.

    Format: 'The enumeration carries it too': keep it as prose and link the rendered listing in the evidence (sections 5.4 and 5.5), which shows the columns stayed aligned.

2026-09-06-distinguish-a-requirement-from-an-example

Records version 0.10.0. This change made the accepted specifications the project's only source of obligations. It also made any agent claim about what the project requires carry a named requirement or a plain statement that the contract is silent. After silence the agent takes one of three allowed routes and never an invented rule. It started from one incident. An agent flattened accepted-specification paths because of a README line that disclaims its own layout, then wrote a false reason for doing so, and every check passed. The only part a machine checks is `review/example-content`: a template's example identifiers warn at validation and block archival and sync. The central assertion rule has no mechanical check; four recorded transcripts are its verification. The change shipped 0.10.0 and `scripts/check-installed`, after finding the installed instruction files stale since 0.6.0. It is also where this migration's own 'Name the requirement, or name the silence' rule comes from, and its after-state transcript is the first record of the rule that nested capability paths are preserved.

Collapsed specification. One capability, so there is no grouping question. Open with the Purpose paragraph, then the five requirements in source order, which is the argument's order: 'The project's obligations are what its accepted specifications state' (what the contract is), 'An assertion about the contract names the requirement it rests on' (what a claim owes), 'Silence is recorded and not filled' (what follows when nothing is owed), 'Generated example content is non-normative and its survival is reported' (the one mechanically checked hazard), and 'Every workflow carries this obligation in one wording' (how the rule reaches agents). Every later requirement depends on the first one's definition of the contract. No renames, so every heading derives its own identifier. The five headings and 24 scenario headings are all distinct.

Purpose statements. The one delta, contract-authority, carries a ## Purpose written by the author. It says the capability defines what states the project's obligations and what does not, what an agent owes when it asserts one, and what it does when the contract is silent. It exists because a README example was cited as a contract with a justification and every check passed, so the repair is a stated obligation rather than a stricter check.

Change subject. Only a little. Because the change created the whole capability, the Purpose nearly states the change's subject. It does not say that this change introduced the capability and that all five requirements are new. A one-sentence subject ('This change introduces the contract-authority capability…') would cover that and would give the specification's header a summary that is not the template placeholder. Its source text already exists in the proposal's first 'What Changes' bullet, so it would not be new content.

Built differs from stated. The archived delta was revised during implementation to match the build: the gate was widened from 'Archival SHALL refuse' to every contract-applying operation (review finding 2), and the workflow count was removed (review finding 6). So for 0.10.0 the delta and the build agree in substance. One difference remains. Requirement 'Generated example content is non-normative and its survival is reported' reports 'a unit whose identifier is one a template writes', but `figure-example` sits on a figure, which is not a semantic unit, and the built rule checks figures alongside units (evidence/the-namespace-decides-the-severity-2026-09-04.md; test `a_figure_carrying_an_example_identifier_is_reported`). The build reports a non-unit the delta's wording does not name. Separately, today's accepted `openspec/specs/contract-authority/spec.md` differs from this delta, because a later change (commit 056df05, PR #28) modified that same requirement to add a placeholder-summary check. That text belongs to the later change. This change's migrated specification.html should be built from the delta as archived, not from today's accepted file.

Evidence and verification units. This change does have verification records that could be cited, but they are uneven. The first three requirements (what the contract is, what an assertion owes, what follows silence) are verified only by reading transcripts: the-guidance-changed-the-transcript-2026-09-06.md and the-obligation-reads-correctly-about-code-2026-09-06.md, over the four files in evidence/transcripts/. The tasks state outright that the assertion rule has no mechanical check. The example-content requirement is verified mechanically: unit tests named in tasks 3.5, 3.6 and 3.8 and in the evidence, the conformance fixture `warning-review-example-content`, and the validate, archive and sync runs recorded in the-namespace-decides-the-severity-2026-09-04.md and the-review-of-pr-20-2026-09-05.md. The one-wording requirement is verified by the pinning test (tasks 4.4 and 4.5; no evidence file records the altered-body failure run) and by the byte-identity note in code-review-pr-20-2026-09-05.md. project-migration's 'A change's delta specifications collapse into that change's one specification' says to omit a unit kind the source did not express. If the migration does omit them, each of the five requirements will draw a `review/unverified-requirement` warning, which the reviewer should expect rather than treat as a fault.

Decided. Decision 5, "Where a change built something other than it stated": this change's specification records what this change built, from the archived delta. The accepted contract-authority is converted as it stands today, and 056df05's later modification of 'Generated example content is non-normative and its survival is reported' belongs to that later change. The reader asked: The accepted `openspec/specs/contract-authority/spec.md` is not this delta. PR #28 (commit 056df05) later modified 'Generated example content is non-normative and its survival is reported'. The coordinator should make sure this change's specification.html comes from the archived delta, and that the later change carries the modification.

    Does: Turns the proposal into five decisions and names the risks it accepts. 2026-09-11-migrate-an-openspec-project

Records version 0.11.0. This change created the project-migration capability and its machinery: `htmlspec migrate survey`, `htmlspec migrate promote`, and a `migrate` workflow. It rests on the premise that every plausible adopter already has an OpenSpec project, and that the obvious file-by-file converter would produce valid documents stripped of their reasoning. Most of its record is its own planning faults caught in flight: stale counts four times, a version composed into archive names that two accepted requirements forbid, a README example read as a layout, and a mapping table that missed 15 files. It also records a deliberate partial self-migration that stopped before writing 60 prose documents, and three post-archival records of nine defects its suite never found. Two of its positions were later superseded by 2026-09-26-record-a-renamed-requirement: renames recorded as an open question and mapped to `modified`, and identifiers keyed per (change, heading). Its gap, that carried HTML evidence was reachable by `validate` and `format`, was closed by 2026-09-29-keep-evidence-out-of-document-discovery, which names this change in its `follows:` key.

Collapsed specification. One capability, so there is nothing to group. Keep the delta's order, which follows the operation: survey, stage order, plan, coverage gate, staging and promotion, checks last. Then come the cross-cutting rules: agent-driven conversion, evidence, the collapse, layout under silence, inexpressible distinctions, already-converted entities, identifiers, versions, and source survival. The Purpose paragraph introduces the requirements. The 15 full-heading identifiers are distinct, the 61 scenario headings are distinct within the delta, and none of the 15 headings was later renamed, so no rename resolution applies.

Purpose statements. One delta, project-migration, carries a '## Purpose' written by its author, not a placeholder. It defines how an existing OpenSpec project becomes an HTMLSpec project (enumeration, reading, a plan before writing, staging, stage order, gating checks), because every adopter already has an OpenSpec project and the obvious file-by-file conversion yields a valid project that has lost its reasoning. It is identical to the accepted spec's current Purpose.

Change subject. Yes, briefly. The Purpose says what the capability is for, not that this change brought it into existence. The masthead should state that this change introduced the project-migration capability, with all 15 requirements and 61 scenarios added. It should say nothing about later revisions: 2026-09-26-record-a-renamed-requirement modified two of these requirements and added one, and 2026-09-29-keep-evidence-out-of-document-discovery modified 'Evidence crosses unchanged'. Those belong to those changes.

Built differs from stated. Four places. (1) 'Evidence crosses unchanged', with 'A source entity already in the destination format is not assumed usable': at archival, `discover::documents` did not exclude evidence/, so `validate` and `assets` reported carried HTML evidence and `format` rewrote one carried file (task 8.5; evidence/migrating-this-repository-2026-09-09.md). The change recorded this as an open question naming its settling change instead of restating the requirement; 2026-09-29-keep-evidence-out-of-document-discovery later settled it. (2) 'Migrated archives carry their versions…' says migration 'SHALL carry the source's release record with it'. As built after the review fixes in the same PR, promotion leaves a destination's existing CHANGELOG.md in place and the shared-version check reads whichever record survives (evidence/three-defects-a-review-found-2026-09-11.md #1; evidence/five-more-defects-a-review-found-2026-09-13.md #3). Where the destination already holds a release record, the source's is not placed. (3) 'A source distinction the destination cannot express is recorded as open, not mapped to the nearest state' says migration 'SHALL NOT map the distinction onto the nearest available value'. The design, the audit, and the staged specifications nonetheless gave renames data-change="modified" with prose naming both headings, plus a plan record. That is consistent with the scenario 'not substituted silently' but in tension with the first paragraph. (4) 'Migration surveys the source…' requires an enumeration derived from what the source holds. At archival the survey missed files loose at three levels; this was fixed before merge on 2026-09-13 (evidence/five-more-defects-a-review-found-2026-09-13.md #1). Point 4 was fixed in the merged code. For points 1 and 2 the coordinator should decide whether this change's migrated specification records the delta's text or the built behavior.

Evidence and verification units. Unlike most changes, this one records verification that could be cited scenario by scenario, as named tests and mutations in the task notes and evidence. Examples: `the_survey_writes_nothing` and `surveying_this_repository_writes_nothing` for 'The survey writes nothing'. `the_survey_is_repeatable_in_the_same_order` for 'The survey is repeatable'. `evidence_nested_deeper_than_the_format_describes_is_enumerated`, with a mutation, for 'Content nested below…'. `removing_one_entity_from_a_complete_plan_fails_the_check` for 'An entity missing from the plan'. `a_deliberate_drop_with_a_reason_is_covered` for 'A deliberate drop passes'. `a_disposition_a_reader_would_disagree_with_passes` for 'The program does not judge a disposition'. `asset_references_resolve_unchanged_across_the_move` for 'Promotion is a move'. `an_abandoned_migration_leaves_the_destination_unchanged_at_every_stage` for 'An abandoned migration'. `a_failed_move_leaves_the_destination_unchanged` for 'A half-migrated destination…'. `a_systematic_mapping_fault_is_reported_as_a_whole_set`, with a mutation. `checking_a_document_while_drafting_it_is_permitted`. `two_headings_deriving_one_identifier_in_one_document_collide`. `one_obligation_renamed_across_changes_is_not_a_collision`. `a_change_recording_no_version_reports_none`. `a_date_and_name_archive_is_accepted`. `a_declaration_below_the_greatest_archived_version_is_refused`. `a_shared_version_the_release_record_explains_is_carried`. Also task 8.4 (a nested path, promoted end to end), task 8.5 (byte identity) and task 8.8 (the gate read 0.10.0 from carried files). 'A migration that only re-wrapped' has only a reading (task 8.7), not a test. The collapse rule forbids deriving units 'from a source document that was not a record of them', and these tasks and evidence files are records of verification. So verification units here would not be invented. Whether to derive them or omit them uniformly is a decision the coordinator should take once and apply to every slice. Evidence units have real sources in all 15 evidence files.

Decided. The plan's decisions and conventions answer each difference, and the 2026-09-09 plan stays evidence, byte-identical and not reused. documents/*.html go to evidence/documents/ (convention 8, "The hand-converted documents cross as they are today"). Every .openspec.yaml is carried, with FOLLOWS written from the survey (decision 1, "Creation dates"). Renames are mapped as renamed-from paragraphs on one identifier (project-migration's "A source rename is carried as the heading the requirement replaced"). The survey at 139b206 lists this change as archived, so no delta is split from its change. Every omitted verification is recorded (convention 6). CHANGELOG.md stays where it is as the release record. The plan's reading lines come from this attempt's readers, and its summary replaces the template's placeholder. The reader asked: The earlier plan (evidence/the-plan-for-this-repository-2026-09-09.html) differs from the brief's central rules and the current migration SKILL in eight ways. (1) documents/*.html: carried, but relocated from `documents/<name>.html` to the same change's `evidence/<name>.html`, on the reasoning 'not usable as a document' (contract 0.1.0, a deleted store), with each file to be 'referenced from the migrated change's design'. The brief leaves this undecided. (2) .openspec.yaml: all eight dropped with one templated reason ('the created date … disagrees with the archive directory name … copied forward'). That reason contradicts itself for 2026-08-31-sync-a-change-into-the-accepted-contract (it reads 2026-08-31, archived 2026-08-31) and for 2026-09-02-state-a-changes-place-in-a-sequence (it reads 2026-09-02, archived 2026-09-02). It says 'archived as migrate-an-openspec-project' of a then-active change. It treats a creation date as an archive date. It predates the `follows:` key now in three later files. (3) Renames: no `renamed:` lines. Each RENAMED FROM and TO heading derives its own identifier. For example, the 2026-08-17-project-bootstrap-cli toolchain-packaging item derives both req-a-single-command-exposes-validate-format-and-init and req-a-single-command-exposes-validate-format-bootstrap-and-create, and the accepted toolchain-packaging item derives req-the-command-surface-names-its-operations-as-openspec-names-them. Staging then set data-change="modified" with prose. The current SKILL requires a renamed-from paragraph, the change state taken from the rest of the delta, and the FROM identifier carried through the whole chain into the accepted spec. (4) The then-active change's delta was sent to `htmlspec/changes/archive/migrate-an-openspec-project/specification.html` while its proposal, design and tasks went to `htmlspec/changes/migrate-an-openspec-project/`. (5) No line records why verification units are omitted, although this change's design says the plan states that reason. (6) No entity for the release record (CHANGELOG.md), which the survey never enumerated. (7) The reading-stage `does:` lines are templated. All 83 evidence entities share one sentence ('A measurement, a transcript, or a recorded complaint — worth having because nobody edited it'). Each change's proposal, design and tasks share one phrase plus a fixed suffix. Every delta reads 'What X established for Y'. Only 114 of 201 lines are distinct, and 42 reasons reduce to 5 templates. This is the plan-written-from-the-listing failure the SKILL names, so the plan cannot stand in for this migration's reading. (8) It keeps the template's placeholder paragraph ('Each task is one unit of work, individually addressable…'). It agrees with the central rules on proposal, design and tasks converted to same-name .html; deltas folded into one specification.html with each Purpose introducing its capability's group; VERSION and evidence carried at the same relative path; accepted specs to `htmlspec/specs/<cap>/spec.html`; and identifiers derived from full headings.

2026-09-15-catch-a-templates-placeholder-prose

Records version 0.12.0. Closed a gap in the example-content rule. The rule matched only template identifiers, so a document whose masthead summary was still the template's "Replace this paragraph…" sentence validated with zero diagnostics and could be archived. The change added the summary as a second site of contract-authority's example-content requirement: whole-summary equality against placeholder text scanned out of the four templates, a warning at validation and a refusal at archival and sync. It kept the deliberate "check the identifier, not the text" sentence and bounded it to units. Its evidence found the defect already sitting in the permanent archive, in the 2026-09-11 migration plan's evidence document, which this change then repaired by one paragraph. Its mutation testing showed that the conformance harness never validates a fixture declaring no rules. The change named that finding and deliberately left it open.

Collapsed specification. One requirement from one capability, so no grouping is needed. The specification holds the single modified requirement 'Generated example content is non-normative and its survival is reported', with data-change="modified" and no rename. It resolves to the same identifier that heading derives in 2026-09-06-distinguish-a-requirement-from-an-example and in the accepted spec (req-generated-example-content-is-non-normative-and-its-survival-is-reported under the plan's derivation rule). Keep its statement paragraphs and all twelve scenarios in source order. A one-sentence introduction drawn from contract-authority's Purpose would tell the reader which capability the requirement belongs to.

Purpose statements. The delta carries no ## Purpose. The accepted contract-authority spec has an authored Purpose: what states the project's obligations, what an assertion about the contract owes, and what to do when the contract is silent, born of a README example cited as a contract.

Change subject. Yes, and here it is required, not optional: this change's own rule reports a specification whose masthead summary is the template's placeholder, so the collapsed specification needs an authored summary. No delta paragraph states that the change extends an existing site, because the delta restates the whole requirement. The summary would say: 'Extends the example-content rule from unit identifiers to a document's summary. A summary that is exactly a template's placeholder text is warned at validation and refused by archival and sync. The identifier rule is kept and bounded to units.'

Built differs from stated. Nothing differs from the delta. The accepted contract-authority requirement is byte-identical to it. `example_content_in` (crates/htmlspec-cli/src/commands.rs:3493) reads the specification's unit identifiers and joined summary for both archival and sync, and validation fires on every kind. The tasks record details the delta leaves open: the summary's paragraphs are joined with a space before comparison (4.3); the scan finds the first header rather than class hs-masthead (3.1); and the scan neither resolves character references nor drops script/style text as the projection does (3.3), which the 3.4 test pins. The one gap is between the proposal and what was built, not between the delta and what was built: the proposal justifies the archival refusal by the permanent record, but the refusal reaches only a change's specification, and the motivating instance was an evidence document.

Evidence and verification units. Real verification exists and can be cited. evidence/mutation-testing-2026-09-13.md shows, for each new scenario, a mutation that breaks it and the named tests that then fail. 'A summary that quotes the placeholder…': mutation 1 fails a_summary_quoting_the_placeholder_reports_nothing, a_summary_quoting_the_placeholder_is_not_reported, and a_specification_quoting_the_placeholder_is_not_refused. 'Every artifact kind': mutation 3 fails every_artifact_kind_carrying_its_placeholder_summary_is_reported. 'A placeholder summary reaching an operation that applies a contract': mutation 5 fails a_placeholder_summary_warns_at_validation_and_refuses_at_archival and the_comparison_refuses_a_placeholder_summary_instead_of_reporting_a_merge. 'A document whose units were replaced…': mutation 4 fails fixture warning-review-placeholder-summary through every_fixture_reports_exactly_the_rules_it_declares. 'A template that rewords its placeholder' is covered only partly: mutation 2b fails the_scanned_placeholder_is_the_projected_summary_of_a_new_document, which pins the scan to the projection but does not test a rewording. 'An absent summary' is covered by a_document_with_no_summary_is_not_reported, and mutation 6 showed that the property holds in is_example_placeholder, not in the guard. An evidence unit could cite evidence/the-gap-measured-2026-09-13.md §1.1 for the requirement's 'measured gap' sentence. The pre-existing identifier-site scenarios were not re-verified by this change.

2026-09-18-establish-a-runbook

Records version 0.13.0. This change gave an html-spec project a fourth place, `htmlspec/runbooks/<name>/`, for a procedure that is run repeatedly. A runbook is a specification plus a tasks document, both of existing kinds. The change was needed because the release procedure had been retyped into five archived tasks documents, all five in the wrong order, and the lesson that corrects the order was written down twice where nothing reads it. The change added `list --runbooks` and creation of the place at bootstrap. It shipped the project's own release runbook at the repository root rather than under `htmlspec/`, because creating `htmlspec/` here would have made this repository a project and turned `self-assets` red. Review of PR #29 then found that `archive` could destroy a runbook. Five added task sections (10 to 14) record the guard, its three fail-open bypasses, and a change-name check. No delta states any of that behavior.

Collapsed specification. One group per capability, runbook-authority first. Introduce it with its Purpose paragraph and keep its six requirements in source order: place, documents, state, version, enumeration, history. That order already runs from what a runbook is to how it is used. Then put project-bootstrap's two modified requirements, introduced by one sentence saying they name the fourth place. runbook-authority goes first because the project-bootstrap delta defers to it by name ('`runbook-authority` states what a runbook is and what it holds; this requirement states only that the project's root has a place for one'), so a reader needs the definition before the layout sentence that refers to it.

Purpose statements. runbook-authority carries an author-written ## Purpose: it defines what a runbook is, where a project keeps one, which document carries authority, and what a runbook does not carry, because a lesson learned at 0.10.0 was rediscovered at 0.12.0. project-bootstrap's delta carries no ## Purpose, and the accepted project-bootstrap Purpose was a TBD placeholder at the time, per the sync evidence.

Change subject. Yes. runbook-authority's Purpose says what the capability is for, not what this change did, and project-bootstrap's delta has no statement at all. A proposed statement: 'This change establishes the runbook: a fourth place beneath a project's root, holding a specification and a tasks document, for a procedure run repeatedly rather than archived. It introduces the runbook-authority capability and modifies two project-bootstrap requirements so that the project's layout and its protection on re-bootstrap name that place.' The statement should not mention the release runbook at the repository root, because that location is the agent's choice under silence and not part of the contract.

Built differs from stated. The built result goes beyond the deltas; it does not contradict them. (1) `archive`, `sync`, and `status --change` refuse a runbook directory and fail closed when the answer is unknowable (tasks 10.2 to 10.4 and 12.2 to 12.4; evidence archival-destroyed-a-runbook-2026-09-17.md and the-guard-failed-open-2026-09-18.md). `new change` refuses a name containing `/`, `\`, `.`, or `..` (task 13.1). No delta requirement or scenario states either behavior, and the sync merged the deltas byte-identical after this work, with 21 scenarios. The nearest delta text is runbook-authority's 'A procedure that is run repeatedly SHALL NOT be represented as a change…' and the scenario 'A procedure that is run again'. After the fixes the build honours both, and before them it violated both. (2) The clause 'A unit in a runbook's canonical documents SHALL declare that it is unchanged' has no mechanical check: validation accepts a violation in either mode (the-canonical-documents-change-state-2026-09-17.md; the-sync-and-the-archival-2026-09-18.md §4.5). The delta does not claim a check, so this is not a divergence, but the migrated specification should not suggest one exists. (3) The built enumeration lists a directory holding one document, or none, as a runbook, which fits the enumeration requirement and strains 'A runbook is two documents of existing kinds'. Whether (1) calls for any text in the migrated specification is an open question. Adding a scenario would add text that no source contains.

Evidence and verification units. The tasks and evidence do record verification, but the source ties only one scenario to a test explicitly. Task 4.4 says the scenario 'An enumeration nobody maintains' is pinned by a test, without naming the test. Other mappings can be inferred from named tests but the source does not state them: `establishing_a_project_creates_the_directories_it_is_made_of` for 'A bootstrapped project has the place' (task 5.3, mutation 5); `the_two_document_split_is_forced_by_validation` for 'A procedure in the canonical document' (task 1.2); `a_runbooks_documents_validate_as_documents_of_their_kinds` for 'A runbook validated by the ordinary path' (task 3.1); the ten list tests for the enumeration scenarios (task 6.6); and `archival_refuses_a_runbook_and_leaves_it_on_disk` for 'A procedure that is run again' (task 10.4). Scenarios such as 'A runbook renamed', 'A runbook's history', 'A version beside the project's', and 'A runbook cited as a project obligation' have no recorded check. Evidence units could honestly cite the nine carried files. Verification units built from the inferred mappings would be derived from a document that did not state them, which is what 'A change's delta specifications collapse into that change's one specification' forbids. Not decided.

Decided. Decision 4, "Where this plan goes, and what the next change must do": the first change after promotion moves runbooks/release/ byte-identical to htmlspec/runbooks/release/, keeps the two retained stylesheet revisions in htmlspec/assets/, and points the self-runbooks stages at htmlspec/; promotion leaves runbooks/ in place. Re-checked at 139b206 in the decision's 2026-10-13 amendment. The reader asked: This repository's own release runbook, `runbooks/release/` (specification.html, tasks.html, VERSION, CHANGELOG.md), is at the repository root. The survey enumerates only `openspec/`, so it is not a surveyed entity. The design's first risk names migrating this repository to `htmlspec/` as what closes the gap between the contracted location and the dogfooded one, and this migration is that event. Once promoted, this repository is a project, and the requirement 'A project has a declared root holding one asset store' as modified here says the project's `htmlspec/` holds its runbooks. The runbook would then sit outside that place, and `scripts/check`'s `self-runbooks` and `self-runbooks-format` stages point at `runbooks/`. The plan must say whether the runbook moves. It is outside this slice and I have not decided it.

Decided. Decision 5, "Where a change built something other than it stated": the specification records what the change built, with a note naming each deviation; behaviour beyond every delta (the runbook refusal in archive, sync and status, the fail-closed default, the change-name check) is a note on the nearest requirement, and no scenario is written that no source contains. The reader asked: Built behavior has no delta text: the runbook refusal in archive, sync, and status, the fail-closed default, and the change-name check. 'A change's delta specifications collapse into that change's one specification' requires the implemented result where it disagrees with a delta. Here the build goes beyond the deltas without disagreeing, so the contract gives no answer, and carrying the behavior would mean writing scenarios no source contains.

Mapped. project-migration's "Identifiers are derived once and every reference resolves through that derivation": derivations.json at 139b206 resolves each heading to one identifier in every slice: the three runbook-authority requirements as above, and the two project-bootstrap headings modified here (req-a-project-has-a-declared-root-holding-one-asset-store, req-bootstrapping-is-repeatable-without-loss) across 2026-08-17, this change and the accepted specification, with no collision. The reader asked: Identifier coordination: requirements introduced here are REMOVED by 2026-09-26-carry-a-runbook-to-another-machine ('A runbook carries no version and no changelog of its own') and MODIFIED by 2026-09-26-log-a-runbook-run ('A runbook records what its history taught', 'The canonical procedure carries no completion state'). The two project-bootstrap headings modified here are restated in later changes too. Every one must resolve to one identifier across the slices.

Decided. Convention 3, "Source paths stay as text, and links go to the migrated counterpart": neither name has a migrated counterpart (no such change, active or archived, at 139b206), so both stay plain text. The reader asked: The successor names `author-a-runbook-through-the-change-lifecycle` and `record-a-runbooks-history`, cited in the proposal, design, and evidence, match no archived or active change. They should stay as plain text, not links.

2026-09-26-carry-a-runbook-to-another-machine

Records version 0.15.0. This change let a runbook run on a machine where its source project is absent, and argued for a contract instead of a bundle. A runbook states what it needs of a machine as ordinary requirement units carrying a `preflight/v1` note. `htmlspec preflight` and `run --as` check those needs before any record exists, and nothing lets a run skip the check. Tools and skills are never vendored. To do this it reversed establish-a-runbook's rule that a runbook carries no version: a carried runbook cannot derive its history from an archive it does not have, so each runbook now has its own VERSION and CHANGELOG.md. The version has an enforcing consumer, because archival compares it against the fingerprinted snapshot in each archive's runbooks.json. This archive is the adoption release (0.15.0) that the planning-root marker names.

Collapsed specification. One group per capability, ordered by the change's argument, not alphabetically. First runbook-portability (4 added), introduced by its Purpose. Then runbook-authority: the removed 'A runbook carries no version and no changelog of its own' placed immediately before its replacement 'A runbook carries an independently checked release version', then 'A machine requirement is still an obligation of the run'. Then project-bootstrap (2 added), the gate that gives the version a consumer. Last, toolchain-packaging (1 added), the command surface. That makes 10 requirement units (9 added, 1 removed) and 38 scenarios in total. A thematic grouping across capabilities (preflight versus release version) would read well but would hide which accepted spec each requirement lands in.

Purpose statements. Only runbook-portability carries a ## Purpose: letting an operator carry a runbook elsewhere and establish its prerequisites before a run, with dependencies kept external and the release identifiable. The runbook-authority, project-bootstrap and toolchain-packaging deltas carry none.

Change subject. Yes. The one Purpose describes a capability, not this change, and no delta says that the change reversed an accepted rule. A statement of the change's subject would say this: a runbook can run on a machine without its source project. It declares machine prerequisites as requirement units carrying a `preflight/v1` note, and preflight and run creation check them before any record exists. Reversing establish-a-runbook's rule, each runbook now carries its own VERSION and CHANGELOG.md, and archival compares them against published runbooks.json snapshots, so the version is enforced and not merely stated.

Built differs from stated. The deltas and the accepted specs for all four capabilities are identical, checked with diff, so the sync applied the text verbatim. Design section 7 and the code record built rules the deltas do not state. (a) Archival skips an archive whose recorded VERSION will not parse, so that archive contributes no snapshot (runbook_release.rs around line 1096, which comments that 'this is a decision the design did not make'), and leaves the reporting to scripts/check-release. That is narrower than project-bootstrap's 'A malformed existing snapshot SHALL be reported, not treated as an absent predecessor' for this case, although a malformed inventory is reported as the delta says. (b) A withdrawn requirement's check declaration is not a check. (c) A declaration on a requirement with no identifier is refused. (d) A staged runbooks.json or VERSION found in an active change refuses archival. (e) A tool found inside a declared input's closure counts as supplied by the pinned environment. Only (a) is in tension with delta text. (b) to (e) add rules beside it. Whether the migrated specification states them is for the reviewer.

Evidence and verification units. None can be cited. The change has no evidence directory. All 31 tasks are checked and each carries a 'verify …' clause, but none records a result, and task 7.3's instruction to record actual outcomes and unrun commands left no trace in the change. Fixtures (fixtures/conformance/valid-runbook-machine-requirements and its -unsatisfiable twin) and tests (crates/htmlspec-cli/tests/preflight.rs and archive.rs) exist in the repository, but they are code, not a record of a run. Deriving verification units from checkboxes would invent a record, so evidence and verification units should be omitted and the plan should record why.

The product reads it at htmlspec/runbook-releases.json, and an inventory without its marker is an error. No requirement states the marker's location, so the plan must place it and record that the contract is silent.

That decision belongs to another slice, but it determines whether this carried record stays true.

    Does: Argues that a portable runbook needs a contract that states what a machine must supply, not a bundle of copies that drift. It uses the project's own record of an unstated precondition that was found by breaking it (init run inside an existing project) and check-installed's drift problem as the cost of vendoring. It concedes to package managers only for the kind of dependency a package manager can express, and it makes a per-runbook version admissible only if a gate compares it.

2026-09-26-log-a-runbook-run

Records version 0.14.0. This change gave a runbook's runs somewhere to go. Before it, a runbook held a procedure but a run left no record, which reproduced the 0.10.0/0.12.0 lesson the runbook existed to fix: nothing could say which version of the procedure a release ran under. The change makes each runbook's specification its runs' logging contract. A run record becomes a `tasks` document under `runs/` that copies the procedure and the requirements, with one `verification` per requirement as the log entry, checked by `htmlspec run --check` through a project-level `review/unrecorded-requirement` rule that never gates. Every part of that shape is argued as forced by measurement and was re-measured before design. The build then went through mutation testing and a two-review repair round, whose fixes (compose-validate-write, a whole-procedure copy, withdrawn requirements excluded) go past what the design describes.

Collapsed specification. One group per capability, runbook-authority first, following the proposal's own order in 'What Changes': the log contract comes first because it is what a run record attests to, so a reader meets the contract before the record. The two `modified` requirements come first within that group, and the five runbook-execution `added` requirements follow in the delta's order (where the record lives, what it carries, its lifecycle, conformance, authority), which already reads as an argument. Introduce each group with one line naming its capability, because neither delta supplies a Purpose paragraph to do it.

Purpose statements. Neither delta carries a `## Purpose`. The accepted openspec/specs/runbook-execution/spec.md has an author-written Purpose ('Defines what a run of a runbook is, where its record lives, what that record must carry, and that the record is history rather than contract…'). It was written at archival from the proposal's Capabilities line and is not in the delta. runbook-authority's accepted Purpose predates this change (establish-a-runbook) and says nothing about runs.

Change subject. Yes. Neither delta says what the change did, and read apart the two capabilities do not say that the record exists to attest to the runbook's own contract. A statement drawn from the proposal's 'What Changes' and 'Capabilities' would serve, for example: 'Gives a runbook's runs a record. A new capability, runbook-execution, states what a run's record is, where it lives, what it carries, how its conformance to the runbook is reported without ever gating, and that it is history rather than contract. runbook-authority is modified so that a runbook's specification states what its runs must record, and so that a run record's units declare themselves unchanged.' The accepted runbook-execution Purpose supplies the first half nearly word for word.

Built differs from stated. Three places, all from the second review round (evidence/the-review-fixes-2026-09-20.md, evidence/the-sweep-2026-09-20.md). None contradicts a delta. (1) A copied requirement the runbook declares `removed` is excluded from the record and from `--check` (finding 11), because a verification naming it would be a `refs/removed-target` error. Read literally, the delta's 'the requirements it attests to' and 'every requirement the runbook states' include a withdrawn one. (2) Only an outcome the schema enumerates, other than `not-run`, counts as attesting (task 4.3, finding 5), so `run`'s own `not-run` entries and a misspelled outcome both report as unrecorded. The delta leaves `not-run` implicit, and the scenario 'A run under way' depends on it. (3) The record copies the procedure's whole `main` content, not just its task units (finding 9, task 11.4). This matches the delta ('the runbook's procedure, copied'): the code was brought into line and no delta was edited. Otherwise the deltas are what was built, and the accepted runbook-execution spec is identical to its delta. Recording (1) and (2) in the migrated specification would add text no delta contains, so whether 'records what was built' requires it is the coordinator's call.

Evidence and verification units. This change has real records that could be cited. Evidence units can point at all seven carried files, each of which is a record. For verification, the source records checks with a method and an outcome, but per scenario rather than per requirement. The guard file checks 'A record offered where a change is expected' and 'A record offered to the comparison' (archive, status, and sync refused, exit 2). The shape file checks 'A record naming a requirement it does not carry' (`refs/unresolved`) and 'A record declaring its copied requirement as added' (`review/stale-verification`). The runbook-ran file records a `run`-produced record that validates and is canonical. The two mutation records show that named tests pin 'A run started over an existing record', 'A run's record created by the operation that starts a run', and 'A run under way'. The deltas carry no verification units. Whether writing verification units from these records is manufacturing them, under 'A change's delta specifications collapse into that change's one specification', is not decided here.

Decided. Convention 3, "Source paths stay as text, and links go to the migrated counterpart": where the design and tasks cite those files by bare name, the text stays and links to the carried file in 2026-09-18-establish-a-runbook/evidence/, its migrated counterpart; the two cited only from inside this change's evidence are untouched. The reader asked: Five evidence files this change's design and tasks cite by bare file name live in another change: `the-status-gap-2026-09-17.md`, `the-canonical-documents-change-state-2026-09-17.md`, `the-guard-failed-open-2026-09-18.md`, `archival-destroyed-a-runbook-2026-09-17.md`, and `the-location-is-blocked-2026-09-17.md`, all in `2026-09-18-establish-a-runbook/evidence/`. The last two are cited only from inside this change's evidence, which crosses unchanged. 'Evidence crosses unchanged' requires a document to reference its own change's carried evidence and says nothing about another change's. A relative link `../2026-09-18-establish-a-runbook/evidence/…` would resolve in the archive layout, but no requirement says to add one.

    Does: Creates the capability's five obligations. (1) A run leaves a record in a place derived from the runbook, created on first write and refused by change operations. (2) The record carries the whole procedure and copied requirements (argued as forced), each `unchanged` and with an outcome and a method, as the kind that carries work. (3) A run is one record, resumable, never overwritten, and carries no timestamp. (4) Conformance is reported per run and requirement, never gates, is evaluated where both documents are in view, and has three exclusions. (5) The record is history, refused by the comparison, and its run count is derived rather than stored.

2026-09-26-record-a-renamed-requirement

Records version 0.16.0. This change let html-spec say that a requirement was renamed. It adds a `renamed-from` paragraph on the requirement, kept separate from its change state so that a requirement renamed and rewritten in one change keeps both facts. Six validation errors bound it, it projects as `renamedFrom`, and the element contract moved to 0.2.0 while still accepting 0.1.0. It also closed a hole its premises check proved: `sync` and archival compared identifiers only, so an unapplied rename was reported as 'applied in full'. They now report untaken renames by comparing heading names. The change was prompted by this very migration, whose earlier plan had to record the toolchain-packaging rename chain as open. It replaced that with the rule that a renamed requirement keeps its first heading's identifier through every change in the chain.

Collapsed specification. Seven requirements: three added (one each in artifact-kinds, document-schema and project-migration) and four modified (two in project-migration, two in toolchain-packaging). They form one feature and cite each other by capability name. For example, toolchain-packaging compares 'heading names ... as document-schema's "A renamed requirement states the heading it replaced" defines'. Use one group per capability, with the definition first: document-schema (the field and the heading name), then artifact-kinds (what an applied rename leaves), toolchain-packaging (how the check detects one not applied), and project-migration (how a source rename crosses). Grouping by capability keeps those capability-qualified citations readable. The arrangement is the agent's under project-migration's 'A change's delta specifications collapse into that change's one specification'.

Purpose statements. None of the four deltas carries a ## Purpose. Each opens directly with ## ADDED or ## MODIFIED Requirements.

Change subject. Yes, briefly. No delta has a Purpose, and a reader of the specification alone sees seven requirements in four capabilities rather than one feature. A short opening would let the specification be read without the proposal, as artifact-kinds' 'A specification states the settled contract as built' requires (scenario 'The contract read without the change'). It could say that this change lets a requirement state the heading it replaced, separately from its change state, and carries that fact through the merge into the accepted contract, the sync and archival check, and migration from OpenSpec. It should not present the 0.2.0 contract version as something a requirement states (see implemented_differs).

Built differs from stated. Nothing built contradicts a delta. The document-schema delta already includes task 1.2's correction (the heading name). Three built results go beyond every delta. (1) `schemaVersion` became a closed set {0.1.0, 0.2.0}, and new documents declare 0.2.0 (design decision 8; what-the-implementation-revealed). No requirement, in the deltas or the accepted specs, states which versions a toolchain accepts. document-template's 'A document declares its identity and provenance' only requires that a version be declared. The contract is silent. (2) The rule that a later change restating a renamed heading resolves to the chain's identifier (the-implementation 7.2) is written in migrate.md, not in the project-migration delta's rename paragraph (see that entity's open question). (3) The 'Renamed from' generated label and the new stylesheet revisions (design decision 7). No delta states them, and none needed to: readability comes from the markup (document-validation's 'No-JavaScript readability is enforced'), and keeping the old revisions is what document-template's 'Documents share one pinned runtime' already requires (scenario 'Two documents needing different bytes of one file').

Evidence and verification units. Unlike most changes, this one's evidence records verification that could be cited requirement by requirement. For document-schema's added requirement: the-implementation 4.1 (six `schema/rename-*` codes, tests seen failing first), 4.2 (twelve valid and invalid twin fixtures, each invalid one reporting exactly its one error), 4.3 (formatting is idempotent), and mutation-testing mutations 1 to 10. For both toolchain-packaging requirements: mutation-testing mutations 11 to 18 name the test behind each rename scenario, including the CLI test `a_change_whose_only_unapplied_work_is_a_rename_has_not_been_synced`, with the-premises 1.1 as the recorded before state. For project-migration's 'Identifiers are derived once…': the-implementation 7.2 and mutation 19 (`one_obligation_renamed_across_changes_is_not_a_collision`). Nothing is recorded for artifact-kinds' rename requirement (agent-driven, implemented by instructions alone), for project-migration's 'A source rename is carried…' (task 7.1 rewrote a migrate.rs test, but no evidence says what it asserts), or for the modified 'recorded as open' requirement. project-migration's collapse requirement says to omit a unit kind and record why rather than manufacture it. These evidence files are records of verification, so whether units citing them count as manufactured is the coordinator's call.

Mapped. project-migration's "A source rename is carried as the heading the requirement replaced": each renaming change carries a renamed-from paragraph on its TO: heading, keeps the identifier derived from the first heading (req-a-single-command-exposes-validate-format-and-init, as derivations.json records with no collision), and carries 2026-08-17's reason paragraph into its migrated specification. The reader asked: This change is the source of the rename rules the migration itself applies. Its evidence (the-implementation 7.2) checked that the toolchain-packaging chain resolves to `req-a-single-command-exposes-validate-format-and-init` in 2026-08-10, 2026-08-14, 2026-08-17, 2026-08-30, 2026-08-31 and the accepted spec. derivations.json matches that table row for row and records no collisions. The two renaming changes' RENAMED sections are in other slices. 2026-08-17's carries an author's reason paragraph that project-migration's 'A source rename is carried as the heading the requirement replaced' now requires the migration to carry.

2026-09-28-confine-the-asset-check-to-the-project

Records version 0.17.0. This change fixed where the duplicate-asset check stops. A project's stores became the ones inside its own htmlspec/ directory. Every other store in the repository is checked on its own and never compared, and the report says which stores were which. It was needed because creating htmlspec/ in this repository, which both the release runbook's move and the self-migration require, turned the self-assets stage red with nine duplicates, none of them the project's. Its own measurement showed the defect was wider than the proposal said: one of the nine was two conformance fixtures against each other. Its evidence pins both halves: zero duplicates in the repository after the change, while a second store planted inside the project still fails. Released as 0.17.0.

Collapsed specification. One requirement with eight scenarios, so there is nothing to arrange across capabilities. Keep the source order: the four scenarios the requirement already had, then the four this change added. That matches the accepted document-validation spec, where the same text sits in the same order.

Purpose statements. None. The one delta holds only a ## MODIFIED Requirements section, so there is no Purpose statement to account for.

Change subject. Not for the collapse, since there is one delta. The requirement's heading is unchanged and does not say what this change did, so the document's subject needs a sentence the delta lacks. For example: 'Fixes where a project's asset stores are: the stores within its own htmlspec/ directory, compared only with one another. Every other store in view is checked on its own and named in the report.' That is drawn from the proposal's 'What Changes' and should be recorded as text the delta does not contain. The requirement's own statements already let a reader determine the obligation without the proposal, as artifact-kinds' 'The contract read without the change' asks.

Built differs from stated. None at the level of the requirement. The accepted document-validation spec holds this delta's text verbatim (the only diff is a trailing blank line). The built code (crates/htmlspec-cli/src/topology.rs partition and check; the payload in commands.rs) matches each statement, and the-measurement section 4.2 observes both halves. Two points for a reviewer, neither a disagreement. (1) The human report names each outside store but gives only a count for the project's stores ('1 store(s) within the project's htmlspec/ were compared'), while the structured payload names both lists. I read 'The report SHALL state which stores it treated as the project's' as met by that, but it is a judgment. (2) The implementation added 'No store outside it was found' specifically to meet this requirement (what-the-implementation-revealed), which moves the build toward the delta, not away from it. Promotion sharing topology::check is a design fact, and the delta does not state it.

Evidence and verification units. This change does record verification that could be cited, unlike most. evidence/the-measurement-2026-09-27.md section 4.2 observes 'A project beside a fixture that carries its own store' (the five outside stores named as checked on their own), 'A project beside a toolchain's source copy of the runtime' (./assets against ./htmlspec/assets), and 'Two stores inside the project' (the planted store reports 8 and exits 1), all in this repository with the built binary. evidence/mutation-testing-2026-09-27.md names the tests that catch each direction. Nothing in the evidence records 'A store outside the project that duplicates within itself'. The CLI test an_outside_store_that_duplicates_within_itself_is_reported exists in crates/htmlspec-cli/tests/cli.rs, but no record in this change names it. The four pre-existing scenarios have no verification record in this change. Whether to author evidence and verification units from these records, or to omit both kinds as the rule's default, is a central decision. See open_questions.

Mapped. project-migration's "A change's delta specifications collapse into that change's one specification", with convention 4, "Per-scenario change states come from the archive itself", as amended: the modified requirement is stated whole, each scenario carrying its own change state and its accepted counterpart's identifier, the states taken from the archive replay and checked against the accepted specification at the archival commit, and the words the change added and deleted marked with ins and del. The replay at 139b206 matches the reader: the first four scenarios unchanged, and the four from "A project beside a fixture that carries its own store" onward added. The same rule serves every MODIFIED delta. The reader asked: The change state of each scenario inside a modified requirement. The delta restates all eight scenarios under MODIFIED without marking which are new. I compared it with the accepted text just before this change (git show dfb2b04^, identical to the 2026-08-13 delta). The first three paragraphs and first four scenarios are unchanged, and the four added paragraphs and four scenarios from 'A project beside a fixture...' onward are new. document-schema's 'Semantic units declare a change state' makes a scenario with no data-change read as 'unchanged', so a migration that marks only the requirement records the four new scenarios as unchanged, which is false. project-migration's 'Change state per requirement' scenario and the skill's mapping table speak only of requirements. The contract is silent on scenarios within a modified requirement, and deriving their state needs a diff against the prior accepted text rather than the delta alone. Decide centrally. The same question arises for every MODIFIED delta in the project.

Decided. Convention 6, "Evidence and verification units only where a record exists", as amended: a verification is written wherever an evidence file records the outcome of checking a requirement or scenario, citing it, for every change alike; one that reached part of it is partial, with unchecked paragraphs, so the planted-second-store check the first review removed returns as partial ("names both locations" unchecked). The reader asked: Verification and evidence units in this change's specification.html: see specification_notes.omitted_unit_kinds. project-migration's rule is to omit a unit kind 'the source format has none of' rather than derive it 'from a source document that was not a record of them'. Here the evidence files are records of exactly that verification, so the rule's reason does not obviously apply. Deciding it per change would make the migrated archive inconsistent, so it needs one answer for all changes.

Decided. Convention 2, "Records are carried as written, and so is disagreement with them": the claim stays as written, with a link to the correcting measurement that says it is a correction. The reader asked: The converted proposal restates a mechanism its own evidence corrects ('all five stores against the new one'; the cross-change record it cites already showed a fixture-against-fixture duplicate after a bare mkdir). The contract is silent on whether a converted proposal may carry an annotation at that claim, as distinct from a link. See the proposal entity.

Mapped. Not a question: the reader found nothing open. The one distinction it names is the predecessor, under project-migration's "A source change's own configuration is surveyed, and its predecessor becomes its declaration": the survey at 139b206 reports no follows: and only a MODIFIED section, so the change has no FOLLOWS, renamed-from, or removed requirement. The reader asked: Nothing in the central rules looks wrong for this slice. There are no documents/*.html, no ## Purpose, no RENAMED or REMOVED sections, and no predecessor declaration.
