2026-09-29-keep-evidence-out-of-document-discovery

Records version 0.18.0. This change gave a change's evidence a place in the contract for the first time: an evidence/ directory directly within an active or archived change. It made that evidence a record rather than a project document, so the directory walk shared by validate, format, and promotion's conformance check passes over it. A record a contributor names is still checked, and format never writes one. It was needed because this repository's own migration was blocked. Two project-migration requirements put HTML records with superseded versions and dead store addresses under evidence/. There, validate raised errors on all of them, format rewrote all seven, and promotion refused. The evidence measures that block before and after the change. It mutation-tests the positional rule, and it records a review finding that the first draft's two new requirements contradicted each other for format.

Collapsed specification. Three requirements, in dependency order. First, artifact-kinds' 'A change's evidence is kept in the change and is not one of its documents' (added), the definition: where evidence lives, and that it is not a document. Second, toolchain-packaging's 'An operation over a directory collects documents and not a change's evidence' (added), the operations that apply the definition, which it cites by heading. Third, project-migration's 'Evidence crosses unchanged' (modified), whose new paragraph applies the definition to promotion. One group per capability, labeled by capability name, since there is no Purpose to introduce any of them. artifact-kinds' reason paragraph cites 'Evidence crosses unchanged', and toolchain-packaging cites artifact-kinds, so both citations become in-document references by identifier.

Purpose statements. None. The artifact-kinds and toolchain-packaging deltas open directly with ## ADDED Requirements, and project-migration with ## MODIFIED Requirements. No delta carries a ## Purpose.

Change subject. Yes. No delta has a Purpose, and each requirement states only part of the change, so a reader of the specification alone needs one statement of what the change did. The proposal's 'What Changes' supplies the content, so none has to be invented. The statement would say four things. A change's evidence now has a stated place in the change. It is a record rather than a document, so directory walks by validate, format, and promotion's conformance check pass over it. A record a contributor names is still checked and never written. Carried evidence no longer gates a migration's promotion.

Built differs from stated. Not in the archived deltas. The one divergence during the change was repaired in the deltas before archival. The first toolchain-packaging text said a named path is 'operated on as named', and the code followed it, rewriting named records against artifact-kinds' 'no operation ... rewrites'. Task 7.1 and what-the-implementation-revealed section 8 record this. The archived delta already says 'checked as named' and adds format's refusal. commands.rs's writing mode refuses through ProjectRoot::is_within_change_evidence. The accepted artifact-kinds and toolchain-packaging texts equal these deltas (diffed), and the accepted 'Evidence crosses unchanged' equals the project-migration delta. The only gap between what was built and what was written is in the design, not a delta: it says ProjectRoot 'gains one method', and two were built.

Evidence and verification units. This change does record verification that could be cited. mutation-testing-2026-09-29.md names the tests that caught each of eight mutations, and tasks 2.1 to 2.3 tie tests to scenario headings. The named tests exist today in crates/htmlspec-cli/tests/cli.rs, tests/promote.rs, src/discover.rs, and src/project.rs. Scenario to test: 'Validating a project that holds HTML evidence' -> validating_a_project_passes_over_a_changes_evidence; 'Formatting leaves evidence untouched' -> formatting_a_project_leaves_a_changes_evidence_byte_identical; 'Naming the evidence directory checks what it holds' -> naming_the_evidence_directory_checks_what_it_holds; 'Formatting a named record is refused' -> formatting_a_named_record_is_refused_and_writes_nothing; 'Outside a project every file is a document' -> outside_a_project_an_evidence_directory_is_walked; 'Evidence nested below the evidence directory' -> evidence_nested_below_the_evidence_directory_is_evidence; 'A capability that happens to be named evidence' -> a_capability_named_evidence_is_still_validated; 'An archived change keeps its evidence' -> an_archived_changes_evidence_is_evidence; 'Carried evidence in the destination format does not gate promotion' -> carried_evidence_in_this_format_does_not_gate_promotion. Two scenarios have no test named by any record. 'Naming an evidence file checks it' has a test, naming_an_evidence_file_checks_it at cli.rs:876, but no record names it. 'A record in this format at a superseded version' is exercised by the a_record() fixture, but no record maps it to a test. evidence-read-as-documents-2026-09-29.md records before-and-after command results that bear on all three requirements. The two older scenarios of 'Evidence crosses unchanged' have no verification in this change. Whether citing these records as verification or evidence units counts as 'deriving units from a document that was not a record of them' is left open (see open_questions).

Decided. Convention 8, "The hand-converted documents cross as they are today": the four documents cross with their current bytes into evidence/documents/, where artifact-kinds' "A change's evidence is kept in the change and is not one of its documents" keeps them out of every check; the plan records the placement as the migration's choice. The reader asked: Interaction with the central decision on documents/*.html. This change's proposal and evidence assume the 2026-09-09 plan's placement of the four hand-converted documents (2026-08-10-html-spec/documents/deterministic-formatting.html and 2026-08-14-separate-artifact-kinds/documents/{proposal,design,tasks}.html) under a change's evidence/. They declare 0.1.0 and name store addresses (3e4014c…, da53340…, e4f5de7…, 0350261…) that a fresh store does not hold, so anywhere other than a change's evidence/ they draw asset/unresolved errors (evidence-read-as-documents-2026-09-29.md), and a staged tree containing them fails promotion's checks. This change's exclusion is what lets them cross at all. The placement itself remains the migration's own choice under 'A source entity already in the destination format is not assumed usable'.

Decided. Convention 6, "Evidence and verification units only where a record exists", as amended: a verification is legitimate where it cites a carried record stating the outcome of checking that requirement or scenario; a check of something nearby gets none, and one that reached part of it is partial. The reader asked: Verification units. The destination specification carries evidence and verification units, and this change's records do record verification, mapped to tests by name (see omitted_unit_kinds). 'A unit kind the source format has none of' says to omit a unit rather than derive it from a document that was not a record of it. These files are records. Whether citing them makes a verification unit legitimate or manufactured is not decided by any requirement I found.

Decided. Convention 3, "Source paths stay as text, and links go to the migrated counterpart": the proposal's citations of 2026-09-11-migrate-an-openspec-project's evidence and tasks keep their text and link to the migrated counterparts in that change. The reader asked: Cross-change evidence. The proposal's founding measurement and its quotation come from 2026-09-11-migrate-an-openspec-project's evidence and tasks, not this change's. 'Evidence is referenced' covers a claim 'its change recorded evidence for' and is silent on linking into another archived change's evidence.

Mapped. project-migration's "A change's delta specifications collapse into that change's one specification", with convention 4, "Per-scenario change states come from the archive itself", as amended: the modified requirement is stated whole, each scenario carrying its own change state and its accepted counterpart's identifier, the states taken from the archive replay and checked against the accepted specification at the archival commit, and the words the change added and deleted marked with ins and del. The replay gives the one new scenario added and the two others unchanged, and the new paragraph's words are marked. The reader asked: Scenario-level change state inside the MODIFIED 'Evidence crosses unchanged': one scenario and one paragraph are new. The destination can mark the scenario added, but only by diffing against the prior accepted text. No requirement decides this.

Mapped. project-migration's "Identifiers are derived once and every reference resolves through that derivation": both headings are derived once, the apostrophe becoming a hyphen under the plan's identifier rule: req-a-change-s-evidence-is-kept-in-the-change-and-is-not-one-of-its-documents and req-an-operation-over-a-directory-collects-documents-and-not-a-change-s-evidence, each the same in this delta and in the accepted artifact-kinds or toolchain-packaging (derivations.json), and every citation uses them. The reader asked: Identifier derivation for headings with an apostrophe ('A change's evidence is kept in the change and is not one of its documents', 'An operation over a directory collects documents and not a change's evidence'). The same rule must produce the same identifier here, in the accepted artifact-kinds and toolchain-packaging specifications, and wherever other documents cite these headings.

2026-10-02-reject-change-markup-inside-a-unit

Records version 0.19.0. This change made HTML's change markup (`ins`, `del`) an error, `schema/change-markup`, wherever it sits inside a semantic unit, wraps one, or is one. The rule covers every kind and every declared contract version. It was needed because the projection reads `del` like `span`. Withdrawn words ran into a normative statement ('nothing elsestore'), a deleted paragraph became a second statement, a deleted link still satisfied a verification, and a `del`-wrapped requirement projected as current, while `validate` exited 0 even under --strict. The change was a deliberate stopgap. It left the projection untouched, moved the document contract to 0.3.0 (release 0.19.0), and rejected `ins` along with `del`, so that the planned successor, mark-the-words-a-modification-changed, could only relax the rule, which it later did. Its count also showed that none of the 116 staged migration documents carried the markup, so the rule could land before the re-stage. Review added the self-unit and foreign-namespace cases, and the fixture generator gained a table that protects four hand-authored fixtures.

Collapsed specification. One requirement, 'Change markup in or around a semantic unit is rejected' (data-change="added"), with its ten scenarios in the delta's order, each added. No grouping beyond the requirement is needed. Its identifier derives from the full heading: req-change-markup-in-or-around-a-semantic-unit-is-rejected. The accepted document-validation specification still holds the same heading, because the successor modified it without renaming it, so this archive, mark-the-words-a-modification-changed's restatement, and the accepted specification share the one identifier. Scenario headings: 'A deleted phrase and an inserted word in one statement', 'A deleted paragraph in a requirement', 'An inserted word with nothing marked as removed', 'Change markup in a nested unit', 'A unit wrapped in change markup', 'A change element that is itself a unit', 'Any unit of any kind', 'A document declaring an earlier contract version', 'Change markup outside every unit', 'A struck-through phrase is not change markup'. Verifications follow the requirement, each linking its carried record: four passed and one partial from the-rule-measured, and one partial from mutation-testing.

Purpose statements. None. The one delta opens directly with ## ADDED Requirements.

Change subject. Yes, one sentence. The delta does not say that the rule's identifier is schema/change-markup, that the document contract moved to 0.3.0 while 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 stay accepted, or that the projection is unchanged. The proposal's 'What Changes' states all three, so nothing has to be invented. The sentence would say that validation now rejects change markup in, around, or as a semantic unit, as schema/change-markup, at every declared version, that the projection is unchanged, and that the contract moves to 0.3.0.

Built differs from stated. No obligation differs, and the review's additions (the self-unit case and foreign namespaces) are already in the delta. Two notes. (1) The `ins` paragraph's reason ('A reader sees words marked as new and cannot see what they replaced') is the one task 7.1 found false beside a del and replaced in the diagnostic. The delta was not revised to match. (2) The delta requires the diagnostic to 'quote the element's text'. what-the-implementation-revealed records that the quote is the element's whitespace-normalized text content, which does not skip script/style/template/noscript as the projection does, and that a wrapped unit's quote includes the identifier from the heading's hs-id span. Both are consistent with the statement.

Evidence and verification units. Verification can be cited. the-rule-measured-2026-10-01.md reaches four scenarios whole ('A deleted phrase and an inserted word in one statement', 'A deleted paragraph in a requirement', 'A unit wrapped in change markup', 'Change markup outside every unit') and 'Any unit of any kind' in part (a verification unit, in a specification). mutation-testing-2026-10-01.md reaches 'A document declaring an earlier contract version' in part, through the 0.1.0 conformance fixture. 'An inserted word with nothing marked as removed', 'Change markup in a nested unit', 'A change element that is itself a unit', and 'A struck-through phrase is not change markup' are reached only by unit-test names, with no test bodies in any record, so no verification is written for them (listed under the mutation-testing entity's open questions). No source text states evidence units.

Decided. The second review settled this on 2026-10-13 (its question 8, "Quoted markup"): every source code span quoting markup must appear as text, and the checker reports one that does not. The reader asked: Every markup quotation listed in format_notes matters more in this slice than usual. The documents are about change markup, and a live del or ins in a task, a decision, or the specification's added requirement is rejected by the very rule they introduce, as the successor amended it. A live class="decision" or class="requirement" inside a quotation would create a unit. The proposal is the one document where live markup outside units would validate, and its quotations must still stay quotations.

  • design.md

    Does: Reasons out where the rule lives and how far it reaches. It is a `schema/*` error, not a review, safety, kind, or projection fault. It walks the parsed tree and reuses `UnitKind::from_class`, so it cannot disagree with the projection about what a unit is. It fires inside a unit, around one, and (added after review) at an element that is itself a unit. It rejects `ins` as 'half a diff' and so that the successor only permits. It stays silent outside units, leaving the summary as an open call for the contributor. It applies at every declared version. The design bumps the contract to 0.3.0 as a minor under the 0.x clause, and fixes the fixture generator's stale sweep, which had already deleted hand-authored fixtures twice.

2026-10-02-see-a-modification-the-merge-did-not-take

Records version 0.21.0. This change made `htmlspec sync` and archival judge each stated requirement by the change state the change declares on it, not by its identifier alone. Before it, a word or scenario nobody merged read as 'applied in full' and ready to archive, while a withdrawal the merge had applied correctly read as absent and unsynced. Both answers were the wrong way round, and a scratch project measured both. The fix only became possible once state-a-modified-requirement-whole required a modified requirement to be stated whole, and it was needed before the migration lands, because the migrated project's merges go through sync. It added the `untakenContent` and `untakenRemovals` sets, a report of positions and identifiers that never carries text, one `reached_in_full` predicate in place of two copies, and a test that the sync instructions name every payload set. The code review added one more case: a changed scenario inside a requirement marked unchanged.

Collapsed specification. One group: toolchain-packaging, with four modified requirements in the delta's order, which is also their order in the accepted toolchain-packaging specification (Archival refuses on the contract and asks about the work; Archival assesses the merge and never performs it; The command surface reports whether a change reached the accepted contract; The workflow instructions carry a stage for applying a change's contract). The defining comparison is the third, and the first cites it by heading. Putting it first would read better, but no requirement decides the order, so keep the source's order and introduce the group with the change-subject paragraph.

Purpose statements. None. The one delta, specs/toolchain-packaging/spec.md, has no ## Purpose.

Change subject. Yes. The delta states four requirements and nothing about what the change did. A summary is needed, for example: 'The comparison that sync and archival share now judges each stated requirement by the change state the change declares on it. The content an added or modified requirement states is compared as text, a withdrawal counts as reached once it is applied, and two new findings report content and withdrawals the accepted specifications have not taken.' It is drawn from the proposal's 'What Changes' and adds no obligation.

Built differs from stated. None found against the delta as archived. Task 7.1 records that the delta was amended in review to match the code-review fix: the `unchanged` bullet's exception, and the scenario 'A scenario changed inside a requirement marked unchanged'. Task 6.3 records that OpenSpec's merge made each block equal the delta word for word. The differences between built and planned that evidence/what-the-implementation-revealed-2026-10-02.md records concern the design (decisions 1, 6 and 7) and the instructions, not the delta's statements.

Evidence and verification units. Verification can be cited. evidence/the-comparison-measured-2026-10-02.md records outcomes against the built change that reach eleven scenarios whole and two in part (listed on that entity). evidence/mutation-testing-2026-10-02.md records a passing test that reaches part of 'Every reported set is worked'. Evidence units can link all seven evidence files. The two measurements made before the change record the defect, not the as-built contract, so no verification is drawn from them.

2026-10-02-state-a-modified-requirement-whole

Records version 0.20.0. This change reversed the contract's partial-update rule. A change's specification must now state a modified requirement whole: every statement and scenario it will hold, each scenario with its own change state and its accepted counterpart's identifier, and a withdrawn scenario stated as `removed`. An accepted scenario left out is a defect that the merging agent reports and does not resolve. It was needed because the partial clause, copied from OpenSpec 1.7.0's sync skill against OpenSpec's own schema, made a withdrawal and a carry-forward read the same, and the archive held both readings in one change (separate-artifact-kinds); the clause also had to go before see-a-modification-the-merge-did-not-take could compare a modification with the accepted text. Nothing in the program changed and the document contract stayed 0.3.0: the rule lives in artifact-kinds and in sync.md and archive.md, which the review tightened to hold a whole requirement unmerged and to stop archival while one is held. It is the origin of the rule this migration's own 'A modified requirement' step applies.

Collapsed specification. One capability, two requirements, in one group under artifact-kinds. Keep the source order: the added “A change's specification states a modified requirement whole” first, because it is the change's subject and the modified requirement cites it by heading ('as … requires'). Then “Every synthesis and every contract update is agent-driven”, marked modified and stated whole with its five scenarios. With no Purpose to introduce the group, the change-subject paragraph does that job.

Purpose statements. The delta carries no ## Purpose.

Change subject. Yes. Neither section says what the change did as a whole. One or two sentences would do: artifact-kinds now requires a change's specification to state a modified requirement whole, with a withdrawn scenario stated as removed and an omitted accepted scenario reported as a defect, and the merge applies a modified requirement as stated instead of applying partial updates. No unit, field, projection, or validation rule is added, so the document contract stays 0.3.0 (proposal 'What Changes', 'Unchanged').

Built differs from stated. Not for the contract. Task 5.3 records that OpenSpec 1.13.1's archive merged each block equal to the delta word for word, the only other edit being a dropped blank line in an unrelated requirement. At instruction level, the build settles what the delta leaves open. sync.md holds the whole modified requirement unmerged in two cases: an accepted scenario neither stated nor marked removed, and an `unchanged` scenario whose text differs from the accepted one. archive.md stops before archiving while a requirement is held, and sync's fold-in step was removed. The delta neither states nor contradicts the hold. The design's decision 6 and its stale-restatement risk say 'report rather than apply' a mismatched scenario, which the build widened to the whole requirement (task 3.2's deviation).

Evidence and verification units. None that can be cited as verifying a requirement or scenario in this delta. The fixture valid-modified-requirement-stated-whole and archive.md's pasted example check that the validator accepts the shape. Their subject is validity, not what a change's specification states or what a merge does, so they reach no scenario here. The instructions test and the-rule-measured-2026-10-02.md check the merge instructions' wording. The scratch project re-run shows, as expected, that no check was added. Task 5.3's record is OpenSpec's programmatic archive merging this delta, not an agent merging under html-spec's instructions. The nearest candidate is the-rule-measured's finding that the served sync and archive bodies name the requirement and no longer say 'partial update', set against the modified requirement's statement that the project supplies the merge's rules as instructions. I did not map it, because no record states it as a check of that requirement. The coordinator may judge it a partial verification.

Mapped. project-migration's "A change's delta specifications collapse into that change's one specification", scenario 'A scenario the block left out and the merge kept': 'Unknown subcommand' and 'Discoverable help' are stated `unchanged`, with the text the accepted specification held after separate-artifact-kinds' merge, not as a note. Convention 7, as amended 2026-10-08, says the same. The reader asked: This change's proposal ('Why now') and evidence/the-measurement-2026-09-30.md §3 record that the first attempt staged separate-artifact-kinds' two kept scenarios, 'Unknown subcommand' and 'Discoverable help', only as a note. Under this change's rule and the skill's 'A modified requirement', they are `unchanged` units. The first attempt's reading for separate-artifact-kinds does not mention them, so the plan for that slice should take them from the replay's KEPT_BY_MERGE and not from the first attempt's staging.

2026-10-04-resolve-a-reference-across-its-change

Records version 0.22.0. This change made the tasks template's own advice true. Before it, a `data-refs` entry resolved only in the document that made it, so a task naming its change's requirement failed `refs/unresolved`, and the contract contradicted itself (document-schema promised an 'accepted spec reachable from it', while runbook-execution called one-document resolution forced). It defines reach by where a document sits: a `Placement` sum type the CLI derives once, with the order own document, then the change's specification, then every accepted specification, where the first place that declares the identifier wins and a withdrawal holds wherever the unit is found. It was needed now because the first migration attempt had drafted 68 unchecked plain links in 56 units as the workaround. Its evidence includes a dry run that converted those links to `data-refs` against the built rule.

Collapsed specification. One group per capability, in the proposal's order, which is also the order of dependency: document-schema (states the resolution rule), document-validation (its validation side, which cites the rule), runbook-execution (one sentence now cites the rule), toolchain-packaging (one scenario). Each group is headed by the capability name only. No delta has a Purpose, and I would invent no introduction. All five requirements are modified, with none added, removed or renamed.

Purpose statements. None of the four deltas carries a ## Purpose.

Change subject. Yes. No delta says what the change did as a whole. One sentence drawn from the proposal's 'What Changes' would do: a `data-refs` reference now resolves beyond its own document, in its change's specification and then in every accepted specification, by where the document sits, and validation, run records and single-document validation are restated to match.

Built differs from stated. null. Task 6.3's note records that OpenSpec's archive modified exactly these five requirements, that 'each merged block equals the delta's word for word, and no other requirement changed'. the-measurement-repeated-2026-10-03.md records that each block differed from the accepted text at HEAD only by this change's edits. The one surprise in the proof (task 5.3's two 'another change' links resolving) agrees with the delta's scenario 'A reference to another change', which says 'only another change's specification declares'.

Evidence and verification units. Some verification can be cited. the-rule-measured-2026-10-03.md §5.1 reaches 'A task references a requirement in its change's specification' and 'A task references a requirement only the accepted contract holds' (document-schema), and, on my reading, 'Validating one document' (toolchain-packaging). what-the-implementation-revealed-2026-10-03.md reaches 'A change with no specification yet' (document-validation). mutation-testing-2026-10-03.md names a passing test for most of the other added scenarios but records nothing of what each asserts (open question). Evidence units in specification.html could link the carried evidence files for these.

Decided. The second review settled this on 2026-10-13 (its question 1, "Scenario identifiers across documents"): one identifier per scenario, qualified in every document that holds it. The reader asked: Identifier collision inside this change's one specification.html. The document-schema block ('Cross-references address units by identifier') and the document-validation block ('Cross-references must resolve') each carry a scenario headed 'Reference to a removed requirement'. Deriving from the heading gives both `scenario-reference-to-a-removed-requirement`, and the first measurement confirms that the migrated accepted document-schema and document-validation each already declare that identifier, in separate documents. Collapsed into one document, the two would share one identifier, which document-schema's 'Every semantic unit has a stable unique identifier' forbids. Each scenario is also owed 'the identifier its accepted counterpart carries'. The skill defines a collision only as two different headings deriving one identifier, so this same-heading case is not covered, and no requirement says which scenario keeps the accepted identifier or how the other is named. Design decision 7 references both. I have not decided it.

Mapped. project-migration's "A source risk's stated settlement is carried as its response", scenario 'A risk without a heading': it stays in prose, with decision 6's words carrying the acceptance. The reader asked: Risk 1 of the design is settled as accepted (decision 6), but its shape bars a risk unit. See the design entity.

Decided. The second review settled this on 2026-10-13 (its question 4, "Test names as evidence"): a test name is not the author's words naming a scenario, and a name-only record supports a verification only where the drafter reads the test at the record's commit. The reader asked: Whether mutation-testing's named passing tests count as verification records. See that entity.

Mapped. project-migration's "A unit the author's words name is referenced wherever the migrated project resolves it": every staged data-refs is checked in the staging location as it will be after promotion, so promotion's checks decide what resolves in this attempt's drafts. §5.3's list, from the first attempt's tree, is a pointer and not a ruling. The reader asked: the-rule-measured-2026-10-03.md §5.3 lists, unit by unit, which of the first attempt's 68 staged cross-document links resolve as data-refs. The coordinator may want it when planning references in other slices. It was measured on the first attempt's staged tree, so this attempt's drafts may differ.

  • design.md

    Does: Decides that a `data-refs` entry resolves through places tried in a fixed order, derived from a document's position by a five-variant `Placement` type. The CLI derives the placement once and hands rules only sets of identifiers. Every boundary is argued against a rejected alternative using the staged-migration counts: why another change is unreachable, why an archived change reaches the live accepted contract (contributor-confirmed, risk accepted), why a withdrawal holds wherever it is found, why an unreadable document is not an empty set, and why review warnings stay within one document.

2026-10-07-mark-the-words-a-modification-changed

Records version 0.23.0. This change gave HTML's `ins` and `del` one meaning in the projected model. A `del`'s content supplies no field anywhere and is recorded as `deletions` on the nearest requirement or scenario, so the normative text is always the current text. It relaxed `reject-change-markup-inside-a-unit`'s blanket refusal to permit the marks only inside a requirement or scenario marked `modified` in a change's specification, decided by the nearest unit and by `Placement`, and it requires a merge to write the current text so validation can refuse any mark left in the accepted contract. It was needed because a modified requirement could not say which of its words changed. A one-word `sync` edit disappeared into an 18-scenario unit, a real deletion projected as text that never existed while `validate` passed, and hand-applied bold leaked into the accepted contract. The staged migration's 34 modified requirements needed a way to show their edits. It also shipped a stylesheet revision that draws `ins` by shape and makes both marks audible, and it moved the contract to 0.4.0 (release 0.23.0).

Collapsed specification. One group per capability, in the order document-schema, document-validation, artifact-kinds: first what the markup means (the projection and deletions), then where it is permitted, then what a merge leaves behind. That is the order of the proposal's 'What Changes', and each later group names the earlier one's requirement by its heading. Within document-schema, put the added 'A deleted word is recorded apart from what a unit states' before the modified projection-specification requirement, whose new list item only points at it. No delta has a Purpose, so each group could open with the proposal's own sentence for that capability, carried as the author's words.

Purpose statements. None. No delta carries a ## Purpose.

Change subject. Yes. No delta says that this change relaxes reject-change-markup-inside-a-unit's blanket refusal; the document-validation block states only the result. No delta says that the contract moves from 0.3.0 to 0.4.0 (release 0.23.0), or that a screen-stylesheet revision and the archive and sync instructions changed without any contract change in document-template or toolchain-packaging. The summary would say that change markup now has one meaning in the model and one permitted place, and that a merge writes the current text. It must not narrate which words of the two modified requirements moved; the marks show that.

Built differs from stated. Two places where the built projection is more specific than the document-schema delta's words. A reviewer should judge them. (1) The delta says 'one entry for each del that no other del encloses'. As built, an empty or whitespace-only del records nothing (design decision 2, task 2.2's an_empty_del_records_nothing, the schema's nonEmptyText items). (2) For a del whose own class names a unit, nested in a requirement, the delta's 'A del belongs to the nearest unit that encloses it' reads as recording it on the requirement. As built (task 10.1, after the review of PR #46), it is that unit, projects from its own content, and no unit records it as a deletion. Projection rule 8.6.1 states both cases and the delta does not. Task 9.3 records that each merged block equals the delta word for word, so the accepted text carries the delta's wording. Everything else built matches the deltas: the rule, the placements, and the comparison.

Evidence and verification units. This change records real verification. evidence/the-change-measured-2026-10-06.md checks four document-schema scenarios ('A word inserted into a statement', 'A deleted word beside an inserted phrase', 'A deleted paragraph', 'A document with no change markup'). It checks one document-validation scenario in full ('A word inserted into a modified requirement') and two in part, and it checks artifact-kinds' 'Markup left in the accepted contract'; that entity's mapped list has the details. tasks.md also records one rule test per document-validation scenario (task 2.4), passing after task 4.1, and a CLI test per placement (task 2.8). Those outcomes are stated in tasks.md, not in a carried record. evidence/mutation-testing-2026-10-06.md names many of those tests as catching mutations, which implies but does not state that they pass. evidence/the-presentation-2026-10-05.md verifies a document-template requirement that this specification does not hold. Each of the eight evidence files can be cited by an evidence unit.

Decided. The second review settled this on 2026-10-13 (its question 8, "Quoted markup"): every source code span quoting markup must appear as text, and the checker reports one that does not. The reader asked: Escaping in document-validation's modified requirement is the main risk. Its scenarios quote `<del>nothing else</del><ins><code>store</code></ins>`, `<del class="decision">`, `<ins><code>sync</code>, </ins>` and `<del>and </del>`. The same requirement will also carry the drafter's live ins and del marking this change's edit. In a scenario marked `modified` in a change's specification, a quotation left unescaped is permitted markup: it validates and projects as a real deletion. Only reading catches it. document-schema's and artifact-kinds' added requirements quote the same markup, and there a live element would at least be refused.

Records version 0.28.0. This change made the migration contract map the vocabulary that nine earlier changes added, instead of recording it as open. That vocabulary is a task's deviation and dropped state, references across a change, partial verifications, a risk's response, and ins/del marks in a modified requirement, which is now stated whole and completed from the source's own merge. It also made the survey read each change's .openspec.yaml, so that follows: becomes FOLLOWS without a second read of the source, and it left the creation date only in the carried file, because the project decided on 2026-10-01 not to record one. It then revised the first attempt's working folder (~/projects/html-spec-migration/: make_decisions.py, stage_carry.py, replay.py, build_packets.py, brief-draft.md, check_draft.py, and a new check_draft_selftest.py). It proved the revision by re-drafting six packets in a scratch copy, which reached 0 checker findings, and it deliberately stopped short of the re-stage. What it hands the re-stage is a worklist, five plan amendments that have not been reviewed, a fixed routine order, and four findings from the proof.

Collapsed specification. A single group, because there is one capability. I would open with the modified 'A source distinction the destination cannot express is recorded as open, not mapped to the nearest state', because its added list names each mapping and the requirement that governs it, so it works as the specification's index. Then the requirements in that list's order: 'A source task is carried in the state its record supports', 'A change's delta specifications collapse into that change's one specification' (modified), 'A check that reached part of what it names is carried as a partial verification', and 'A source risk's stated settlement is carried as its response'. The two mappings the list does not name come last: 'A unit the author's words name is referenced wherever the migrated project resolves it' and 'A source change's own configuration is surveyed, and its predecessor becomes its declaration'. Keeping the source's ADDED-then-MODIFIED order is also defensible. The arrangement is the agent's.

2026-10-08-record-a-partial-verification

Records version 0.26.0. This change gave a verification a fifth outcome, `partial`. It covers a check that ran against the right requirement or scenario, reached part of it, and found that part to hold. The change also made a `partial` verification invalid unless one or more `unchecked` paragraphs name each part left unchecked. It was needed because the project's own staged migration showed that the four existing outcomes forced reviewers either to overstate such a check as `passed` (twice) or to delete its record (twice). It also restated the unverified-requirement warning so that a verification of any outcome, `partial` included, clears it, moved the document contract 0.5.0 to 0.6.0 and the screen stylesheet to a revision that labels `partial`, and released 0.26.0. It is the requirement the present migration's partial-verification mapping rests on, so this change's own specification is where that vocabulary is first defined.

Collapsed specification. One group per capability. document-schema's added requirement 'A partial verification states what it did not check' comes first, because document-validation's restated requirement names `partial` and depends on the value existing. document-validation's modified 'A specification requirement without verification is reported as incomplete' follows. With no Purpose paragraphs, each group is introduced by its capability's name alone.

Purpose statements. Neither delta carries a ## Purpose.

Change subject. Yes. No delta states what the change did as a whole. The summary would say: the change adds a fifth verification outcome, `partial`, for a check of the right thing that stopped short; requires a `partial` verification to name each unreached part in `unchecked` paragraphs; and states that a verification of any outcome, `partial` included, clears the unverified-requirement warning. Source: the proposal's 'What Changes'.

Evidence and verification units. The evidence records checks that can be cited as verification units (see the mapped entries on the-change-measured and mutation-testing). document-schema: 'A partial verification that does not say what it left', 'An unmarked paragraph does not state it', 'Two parts left unchecked', and 'Any other outcome without it' are reached whole. 'A check that reached part of its scenario' is reached, with a GIVEN caveat. 'A failed check that says what it did not reach' is reached by no evidence file: variant d is `passed`+`unchecked`, a different condition, and only tasks.md's record of task 2.1 and 4.2 says the unit test `a_failed_verification_may_state_what_it_did_not_reach` exists and passed. document-validation: 'A requirement with no verification' and 'Verification is not a gate' are reached whole. 'A requirement whose check failed' and 'A requirement verified only in part' are reached, with the stale-warning caveat. 'A fully verified specification' is not reached, because every scratch variant reports other warnings, so 'nothing is reported' is not shown. 'An unverified requirement in a proposal' has no record. The evidence files themselves can be cited as evidence units for the proposal's measurements.

2026-10-08-record-a-task-done-differently

Records version 0.25.0. This change gave html-spec a way to record a task finished otherwise than its words say: one `deviation` paragraph on a `done` task. Validation refuses it on any other state and refuses a second one, and `list` and `status` count it apart without changing any existing count. It was needed because both encodings available before misreported, a note reading as done as written and `dropped` reading as abandoned, and because the first migration attempt held 33 such tasks it could carry only as notes. It moved the document contract from 0.4.0 to 0.5.0 and shipped as 0.25.0. Its own tasks record ten departures from their words, and its design carries four dated corrections made when the code was re-read six changes after the design was written.

Collapsed specification. One group per capability, document-schema first. Its requirement defines the deviation that both toolchain-packaging requirements count ('as document-schema's "A task declares completion state" defines one'), so the definition should precede the requirements that use it. Within toolchain-packaging, keep the delta's order, the enumeration and then the completion report, because the second says its count is 'the one the enumeration of changes carries'.

Purpose statements. Neither delta carries a ## Purpose. Each holds only ## MODIFIED Requirements.

Change subject. Yes, one or two sentences, because no delta says what the change did as a whole: a `done` task may now state a deviation, which validation confines to one per `done` task, and which the listing and the completion report count apart from the per-state counts. The contract's move to 0.5.0 and the template's example task are in no delta. The summary may state the version move as a fact (tasks 3.3, evidence/the-change-measured-2026-10-08.md), but it is not an obligation.

Built differs from stated. Nothing built contradicts a delta, and task 8.3 records that archival's merged blocks equal the deltas word for word. The deltas are silent on two built details, both kept as built by the contributor at task 9.1. (1) The rule also reports a deviation on a task that declares no state (evidence/what-the-implementation-revealed-2026-10-08.md). Such a document is already invalid for its missing state, so only the diagnostic count differs. (2) The listing's column is absent, not blank, when no row has a count, which is what toolchain-packaging's 'SHALL NOT be shown where it is zero' requires anyway. No source states (1) as an obligation. Whether the migrated specification mentions it is for review.

Evidence and verification units. Yes, verification is citable. evidence/the-change-measured-2026-10-08.md records outcomes against the built change that reach these scenarios whole: document-schema's 'A task done another way than its words say', 'A task done as its words say', 'A deviation on a dropped task', and 'Two deviations in one task'; and toolchain-packaging's 'A change with a task done differently' (under both requirements), 'A deviation leaves the per-state counts whole', 'A deviation on a task that is not done', and 'The enumeration and the completion report agree'. It reaches part of 'A deviation on a task not yet done' (`todo`, not `in-progress`) and part of 'A change whose every task was done as written' (the human row, not the enumeration's payload). No carried record checks 'A deviation outside a task', 'A task that declares no state', 'Archival and the report agree', or the unchanged scenarios. mutation-testing-2026-10-08.md checks the tests, not the scenarios.

So the outcomes tasks 2.1, 2.3, and 4.2 record back no verification. The reader asked: tasks.md records outcomes of checks that no evidence file carries. Task 2.1: `section_4_0_a_deviation_outside_a_task_names_no_field_of_its_unit` passes 'over all six other units', which reaches 'A deviation outside a task'. Tasks 2.3 and 4.2: `a_deviation_on_an_in_progress_task_is_reported` passes after 4.2, which would complete 'A deviation on a task not yet done'. project-migration's 'A check that reached part of what it names is carried as a partial verification' and the skill say 'a carried record'. tasks.md is converted, not carried, so I mapped no verification from it. 2026-10-08-record-how-a-risk-was-settled

Records version 0.27.0. This change gave a risk unit a declared settlement: a `data-response` attribute, `mitigated` or `accepted`, defaulting to `mitigated`, projected into a `response` field every risk carries. A mitigation is now required only of a `mitigated` risk, enforced by a new validator rule, `schema/missing-mitigation`. The document contract moved from 0.6.0 to 0.7.0, shipped in toolchain 0.27.0. It was needed because the contract required a mitigation of every risk, so an accepted risk validated only with a mitigation paragraph denying it was one, which is exactly what the project's own release runbook does. Three of the first migration's readers met the gap independently. Its own measurement bounds the payoff honestly: the missing value blocked only 5 headed risks in the archive, because shape keeps most of the archive's risks as prose. Even so, the migration's handling of a risk's response rests on the requirement it added.

Collapsed specification. There is one requirement, 'A risk records how it was settled', `data-change="added"`. Its seven added scenarios keep the delta's order: a mitigated risk; one written before the attribute existed; mitigated with no mitigation (invalid); accepted with no mitigation; accepted with a partial measure; `partial` (invalid); a response on another unit. The order runs from valid to invalid within each response, so keep it. No grouping is needed for one capability and one requirement.

Purpose statements. None. The single delta carries no `## Purpose`.

Change subject. Yes. No delta prose says what the change did. The specification's subject should say that it adds 'A risk records how it was settled' to document-schema and modifies no accepted requirement. The proposal's 'Capabilities' section gives the reason for that shape, and the subject can cite it: no accepted requirement stated a risk's parts, which lived only in the schema and projection section 4.7. 'Semantic units are identified by class' lists only class names. 'The HTML-to-model projection is published as a normative specification' is not a catalogue of attributes.

Evidence and verification units. evidence/the-change-measured-2026-10-08.md records check outcomes that reach four scenarios whole: 'An accepted risk with no mitigation', 'An accepted risk that names a partial measure', 'A risk written before the response attribute existed', and, with a caveat, 'A response on another unit'. It reaches two in part: 'A mitigated risk with no mitigation', default branch only, and 'A mitigated risk', response but not validity. See that entity's mapped list. Two outcomes are in tasks.md and not in any evidence file. The declared-`mitigated` branch is task 2.3's test `a_risk_declared_mitigated_with_no_mitigation_is_reported` and task 2.5's fixture `invalid-schema-missing-mitigation`. The scenario 'A risk that is partly held down' is task 5.1's record that `invalid-schema-unknown-response` reports `"partial" is not one of "mitigated" or "accepted"`. Whether a task's own record counts as a carried record a verification may cite is for the coordinator. The two pre-change measurements check HEAD, not the requirement. The mutation run checks the tests. Neither verifies a scenario.

Mapped. project-migration's "A source change's own configuration is surveyed, and its predecessor becomes its declaration": a configuration with no `follows:` gives no FOLLOWS, and no predecessor is inferred from prose, names, or dates. artifact-kinds' "A change states the change it follows" forbids the same inference. The stack order stays in the author's prose, carried as written. The reader asked: Predecessor: the design, tasks, and evidence describe this change as built third in a stack of four, but its `.openspec.yaml` states no `follows:`. The survey reports none, so the change gets no FOLLOWS, and the skill forbids inferring one. The reviewer should know the prose and the configuration disagree.

Decided. Convention 6, Evidence and verification units only where a record exists: a verification is written only where an evidence file records the outcome. project-migration's "A check that reached part of what it names is carried as a partial verification" still writes one only from a carried record, and tasks.md is converted, not carried. So the declared-`mitigated` branch of 'A mitigated risk with no mitigation' and the whole of 'A risk that is partly held down' stay unverified. The record of the default branch stays `partial`. 2026-10-08-show-what-a-modification-changed

Records version 0.24.0. This change gave html-spec `htmlspec show <change> --diff`. The command is a read-only view that sets each requirement `sync` compares beside its accepted counterpart. It pairs paragraphs by equality and then by at least half their words in common, pairs scenarios by identifier, and marks changed words as `{+ +}` and `[- -]`. It uses an author's `ins`/`del` only where reading them back reproduces the accepted text. It refuses archived changes and the bare `show`. It was needed because html-spec restates a modified requirement whole, which can be up to 15 paragraphs and 18 scenarios, and a reviewer had no way to find a one-word edit that OpenSpec's `show --diff` finds. The view shares `sync`'s pairing and content comparison so that the two cannot disagree. The change also fixes `show` and `--diff` as OpenSpec spellings in toolchain-packaging. It released 0.24.0 with the document contract unchanged. Reading the code as built (task 1.1) widened the scope before any code was written: the view compares what `sync` compares, including `added` requirements and `unchanged` ones holding a changed scenario, not `modified` alone.

Collapsed specification. One group, toolchain-packaging, introduced by one sentence. Put the added view requirement first, as the delta does: it is the change's subject, and the modified naming requirement only fixes the spellings, `show` and `--diff`, that the new requirement uses. Within the added requirement, keep the delta's order. It runs from what the view shows and why, through each rule in turn: read-only, parity with the reporting operation, statements, words, marks, scenarios, held-by-none and held-as-stated, listed, not merge text, the bare form, archived changes, refusals and exit codes, and structured output with --store. The 21 scenarios follow that order.

Purpose statements. None. The one delta carries no ## Purpose. It holds only ## ADDED Requirements (one requirement) and ## MODIFIED Requirements (one requirement).

Change subject. Yes. No delta says what the change did as a whole. The statement should say three things. The change adds `htmlspec show <change> --diff`, a read-only view of each requirement `sync` compares beside the accepted one, built on `sync`'s own pairing and comparison, and adds `show` and `--diff` to the OpenSpec spellings. It applies to a change before its merge, not to an archived one. The document contract (0.4.0) does not move. The proposal's What Changes holds all of this.

Built differs from stated. Nothing found that departs from the delta's words. Two places where the record narrows or extends the built behaviour. (1) Task 9.1 added a text fallback for a withdrawn scenario with no identifier, which the delta's 'saying whether the accepted requirement still holds it' permits. It also kept as built a case where an accepted scenario carries the withdrawn scenario's identifier but another stated scenario keeps its text: the view says 'no longer held' to agree with `sync`, and a reviewer may weigh that against 'still holds it'. (2) The contributor confirmed the half-words threshold on 2026-10-08 against the 34-case measurement, and it was built as stated.

Evidence and verification units. Verification can be cited. evidence/the-view-measured-2026-10-07.md records passed checks of "A one-word modification", "The author's marks leave part of the difference unmarked", "An archived change", and "Showing a change without a view". It records partial checks of "The view writes nothing" (one change, one outcome), "The author's marks account for the difference" (no del), and "A structured view" (payload-only stdout and the compared specification not stated). evidence/what-the-implementation-revealed-2026-10-07.md records the parity test passing for "The view and the reporting operation agree". For the modified naming requirement, only task 5.3's record supports verification: `--help` lists `show`, `show --help` documents `--diff`, and the naming test names both. That bears on "An operation OpenSpec also provides", "The selectors carry OpenSpec's spellings", and "Discoverable help", but no evidence file records it. The task records name per-scenario unit tests (2.3) and full-suite passes (5.4: 644; 7.4: 1,286), which are tasks-document records, not evidence files.

2026-10-09-fill-only-the-references-a-document-loads

Records version 0.28.1. This change stopped `htmlspec format` from rewriting an author's words. The formatter found asset references by searching for `href="` and `src="`. So it filled quoted markup in <code> and escaped examples, and hyperlinks, while missing <object data>. That broke "Formatting preserves meaning", and the self-migration's drafters had twice mangled markup to get past it. The change moved the asset rules' thirteen loading attributes into htmlspec-assets for both programs to read. It replaced the search with a private scanner that follows the HTML tokenizer, and, after a review, the pinned parser's foreign content and script escape states. It held the scanner to the parsed tree with corpus and property tests, and wrote the fill and its bounds into the requirement. It shipped as patch 0.28.1. It was archived before its review, so task 7.1, part of design decision 2, a risk, and two evidence sections were written into the archive afterwards.

Collapsed specification. One requirement, three statement paragraphs, seven scenarios, so nothing needs arranging across capabilities. Keep the source order: the four scenarios the requirement already held, then the three this change added, as the accepted deterministic-formatting specification holds them.

Purpose statements. None. The one delta holds only a ## MODIFIED Requirements section, so there is no Purpose to account for.

Change subject. Yes. The heading is unchanged and does not say what the change did, so the document's subject needs a sentence the delta does not contain. Drawn from the proposal's 'What Changes', it would say: 'States formatting's one exception to preserving attribute values — filling an asset reference that names bytes the store does not hold — and bounds it to the attributes through which an element loads an asset, the ones the asset rules judge, so hyperlinks and text that quotes a reference are left as written.' Record it as text the delta does not contain.

Built differs from stated. Not at the level of the text. The accepted spec at 139b206 holds the delta's requirement verbatim, bar a trailing blank line, and task 6.3 records that the merge equals the delta word for word. The review's fixes, which landed after archival, changed code, the design and the evidence, and not the requirement. One point for a reviewer, which I have not decided. The requirement says without qualification that 'the formatter and the validator SHALL NOT disagree about which values are references'. The design's first risk accepts that the scanner and the tree disagree on documents whose parse recovered errors (an <img> inside <select>), defended by `format` refusing such documents and writing nothing. Design decision 2 also notes that `rewrite` runs before that refusal, and the migration's staged-document check reports fills beside it. The design's second risk likewise holds no agreement on character references, which the tree decodes and the scanner does not. Whether these make the built result differ from the stated requirement is a judgment the plan's review should make.

Evidence and verification units. This change records verification that could be cited. evidence/the-change-measured-2026-10-09.md section 1 reaches the whole of 'Prose that quotes an asset reference' and of 'A hyperlink to an asset', both passed. evidence/what-the-implementation-revealed-2026-10-09.md sections 1 and 6 record the cross-check behind the requirement's 'SHALL NOT disagree' statement, reaching documents read without error and not those parsed with errors: a partial. No record reaches 'A reference that names stored bytes': no run had a store holding a newer revision. No record reaches the four scenarios the requirement already held. evidence/mutation-testing-2026-10-09.md measures how strong the tests are, not a scenario's outcome. evidence/the-measurement-2026-10-09.md records the defect at HEAD, not the built result.

No risk unit and no `data-response` are written. The first attempt's reports that recommended risk units for this shape predate the requirement, which now settles it the same way in every slice. The reader asked: Risks with no heading of their own. The design's four risks are list lines of the shape `- **[label]** → text`, each with its statement and measure in one line. project-migration's "A source risk's stated settlement is carried as its response" (scenario "A risk without a heading") keeps them in prose, so I mapped no risk response. The first attempt's reports for older archives, for example 2026-09-28, recommended risk units for the same shape before that requirement existed. The coordinator should apply one rule across slices.

Decide centrally, because other slices will meet the same case.

    Does: Finds where text gets in: the substring `find` in `rewrite`'s walk, which cannot tell a tag from the text around it. It keeps the rewrite textual for the reason the module already gives. It decides four things. (1) The thirteen loading-attribute pairs move to htmlspec-assets as one shared type, rejecting both a third copy and a formatter that depends on the validator. (2) A private scanner reads tags as the HTML tokenizer does: comments, CDATA, end tags, quoting, first duplicate wins, raw-text elements, template, and cut-off tags. After review it also follows the pinned parser's foreign content and a script's escape states, with one case where the parser and not the HTML specification decides (annotation-xml). (3) The parsed tree is the oracle, through corpus and property tests in the validator's own test module. (4) The rewrite's report types stay as they are. Its risk list accepts disagreement on documents parsed with errors and on character references, and records the review's correction. The design was edited after archival: two '(Added at review.)' markers and the third risk.

(a) The raw-text bullet's script escape states ("inside `<!--`, a `<script` postpones the end tag until its own `</script` has passed, and `-->` returns to plain script text"). (b) The foreign-content bullet's integration points. Make a table with one row each: SVG (`foreignObject`, `desc` and `title` read children as HTML); MathML (`mi`, `mo`, `mn`, `ms` and `mtext` read children as HTML; `mglyph` and `malignmark` stay MathML); `annotation-xml` (no integration point in the pinned parser, although the HTML specification makes one with an HTML `encoding`); an `svg` directly inside `annotation-xml` (SVG).     Format: Decision 2 quotes markup densely, and some of it is dangerous live: `<!-->`, `<!--->`, `-->`, `--!>`, `]]>`, `<!--`, `<script`, `</script`, `<template>`, `<svg>`, `<math>`, `<`, `>`. Escape every `<` inside <code>. A literal `<!--` opens a comment that swallows the rest of the document. A literal `<script` or `<template>` opens a raw-text or template element. The parser would read the result as structure, and nothing would report it.

  • proposal.md

    Does: Argues that `htmlspec format` breaks deterministic-formatting's "Formatting preserves meaning" by finding asset references with a substring search for `href="` and `src="`. It therefore fills quoted markup in prose and hyperlinks, and misses `<object data>`. It measures four fills on one scratch document at HEAD: three in the author's words, one in an `<a href>`. It traces the fault to two lists that disagree, the formatter's and the asset rules', and argues urgency from the self-migration's drafters, who twice mangled markup to get past it. It scopes the fix as one shared attribute list, a tag reading in the tokenizer's terms, a rewrite that stays textual, a test against the parsed tree, and a requirement that states the fill and its bounds. It also fixes what does not move: when a fill happens, the stored-bytes refusal, the contract version, and every committed document.

2026-10-12-name-each-command-by-its-request-verb

Records version 0.29.0. This change gave every htmlspec operation a second spelling: one of htmx's five request verbs (get, post, put, patch, delete) followed by an object. The verb is chosen by the most the operation writes in any invocation, so `get` promises that nothing is ever written. The OpenSpec spellings stay fixed and primary in the program's messages and in the installed instructions. It was needed because a command's name says what it is about but not whether it changes the tree, and because `sync` and `archive` bring over an OpenSpec expectation, that they write the accepted specifications, which is wrong here. The change modifies one toolchain-packaging requirement (two paragraphs, five scenarios) and is built as a closed `Operation` table plus an `Invocation` router. It shipped as 0.29.0. Its evidence measures what each of 19 operations writes across 42 invocations, first under the OpenSpec spellings and then under both.

Collapsed specification. One requirement, so it needs no grouping. State it whole as `modified`, its paragraphs in the source's order, with the two added paragraphs after 'Fixing a spelling…'. Then the scenarios in the delta's order: the 18 the proposal calls the accepted text, unchanged, followed by the five added scenarios. A short introduction naming toolchain-packaging is all the arrangement needs.

Purpose statements. None. The one delta carries no ## Purpose. It holds only ## MODIFIED Requirements, with one requirement.

Change subject. Yes, one or two sentences. The delta holds one restated requirement and states nothing about what the change did. A sentence drawn from the proposal's 'Capabilities' would say that the change gives every operation a second, request-verb spelling (get, post, put, patch or delete, followed by an object), keeps the OpenSpec spellings fixed and named by the program and its instructions, adds five scenarios, and leaves the document contract at 0.7.0.

Built differs from stated. One candidate, which I have not decided. The second added paragraph says a request-verb spelling 'SHALL produce the same output and exit status'. evidence/what-the-implementation-revealed-2026-10-09.md section 5 records that where clap refuses the arguments before any operation runs, the exit status is the same (2) but the usage line names the spelling typed (`Usage: htmlspec get validity …` against `Usage: htmlspec validate …`). In task 7.1 the contributor declined to change this, reading the requirement as covering the invocations that reach an operation. Otherwise the tasks and evidence show the built result matching the delta: `show` became `get show` (task 1.0), and archival merged the block, adding 24 lines and removing none (task 6.3).

Evidence and verification units. Partial ones only. evidence/the-change-measured-2026-10-09.md records checks under the request-verb spelling that reach part of three of the five added scenarios: 'A request-verb spelling runs the same operation' (exit status, not the report), 'A get operation writes nothing' (all 25 `get` invocations tried, not every option), and 'An option keeps its meaning under the verb' (nothing written and exit 1, not the report). 'The program names the OpenSpec spelling' and 'Every operation has both spellings' have no carried record of an outcome. The source scan, the help tests and the parity tests are reported only in tasks.md notes. mutation-testing-2026-10-09.md records what the tests catch, not a scenario's outcome. the-measurement-repeated-2026-10-09.md ran before the verbs existed, so it reaches no scenario that names a verb.

  • design.md

    Does: Fixes the rule that a verb names the most an operation writes in any invocation, so `get` is a promise about every invocation and an option means the same under both spellings. It fixes each operation's object by a table, not by a rule, and specifies a closed `Operation` type whose exhaustive matches stop a later operation compiling without both spellings. It records each rejected alternative with who rejected it: replacing the OpenSpec spellings, putting the verbs in the instructions, judging by the default invocation (which would have made `migrate promote` a `get`), `get` for every `--check`, the `hx-` prefix, and rewriting argv before clap. It also records the review that moved `init` from `post` to `put` and the `store` operations to `registration`.

  • proposal.md

    Does: Argues that command names hide whether an operation writes (9 of 18 never do, and `status` and `format` read alike), and that the shared spellings `sync` and `archive` carry a wrong OpenSpec expectation of writing the accepted specifications. It proposes borrowing htmx's five request verbs, with HTTP's meanings, as a second spelling chosen by the most each operation writes, keeps the OpenSpec spellings primary so none of the 300 instruction lines changes, and records the contributor's choices of 2026-10-05 (the verb-and-object form, keep every spelling) and 2026-10-06 (`put project`, `registration`).
